"The U.S. tech sector offers global competitiveness unparalleled to any country in the world," Wandji added. "We deliver innovation, transparency and accountability in our business offerings, while creating new markets for U.S. companies."

Convalt’s Achuthan told Fox News Digital what’s working for U.S. business in Africa, "American companies must clearly communicate the value of quality, transparency, safety, responsible business practices and long-term community partnership. Competing solely on price is not enough going forward. Companies from the United States should compete on performance, reliability, innovation, institutional trust and the ability to create sustainable local economic benefits."
Paul Tilsley is a veteran correspondent who has reported from four continents for more than three decades. Based in Johannesburg, South Africa, he can be followed on X @paultilsley.

title: Famed mountaineer Nirmal Purja, 43, among 10 climbers killed after avalanche in Pakistan
summary: Nirmal Purja was leading climbers up Broad Peak in Pakistan when a deadly avalanche struck the Karakoram expedition, killing all 10 members of the group.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Claudia Cowan reports on the deadly avalanche near Castle Peak, Calif., where eight skiers have been confirmed dead. Mike Tobin warns there is 'not a lot of reason for optimism' in recovery efforts on ‘The Story.’
Famous mountaineer Nirmal Purja, who was the subject of a 2021 Netflix documentary, was among 10 climbers confirmed dead on Saturday on the world’s 12th-tallest mountain in Pakistan.
The climbers were killed when they were hit by an avalanche on the 26,414-foot-tall Broad Peak Thursday in the Karakoram mountain range.

"The world has lost one of mountaineering's greatest climbers," Elite Exped, the company involved in the expedition, said in a statement, adding, "we mourn not only Nims, but every life lost in this tragedy."
AMERICAN CLIMBER'S REMAINS FOUND AFTER AVALANCHE IN PAKISTAN, OTHER MOUNTAINEERS STILL MISSING

Nirmal Purja speaks during a news conference in Kathmandu, Nepal, on May 28, 2019, after climbing six mountains including Mount Everest as part of an attempt to climb fourteen 8,000-meter peaks in seven months. (REUTERS)
The company added, "No words can ease the pain of this unimaginable loss."
Purja had been leading the group up Broad Peak.

A Pakistani rescue team recovered three bodies on Friday, including American Sarah Mallory Geis, but had to temporarily halt the operation in the "remote and difficult" area due to weather conditions.
NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS
The search resumed on Saturday and rescuers are attempting to recover the remaining seven bodies.

"The loss of these courageous climbers, who came from different nations united by their passion for the mountains, is an immeasurable loss to the global mountaineering fraternity," Irfan Arshad Khan, the president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, said.
The climbers were ascending Broad Peak, the world's 12th tallest mountain in the Karakoram range of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. (AFP via Getty Images)

"The mountains inspire us with their beauty, but they also remind us of the immense risks faced by those who venture into the high Himalaya and Karakoram," he added, thanking the military, Sherpas and civilians who took part in the rescue mission.
Along with Purja, who was British-Nepali, and Geis, the other climbers were from Pakistan, Nepal and China.
Purja was featured in the 2021 Netflix documentary "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible" in which he attempted to summit the world’s 14 tallest mountains in seven months.

Nirmal Purja, one of the members of the all-Nepalese mountaineering team that became the first to scale Mount K2 in winter, gestures as the team arrives at Tribhuwan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal, on Jan. 26, 2021. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

British Defense Minister Wes Streeting called Purja an "inspirational ​man who served in our Armed Forces for many years — and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."
The 43-year-old had served in the British army with the Gurkhas, Nepali soldiers recruited to serve with the U.K., and he later served in the British special forces.

title: State Department raises travel warning for part of Spain as migrant surge sparks military deployment
summary: Tens of thousands of migrants surged into Spain's Ceuta from Morocco, prompting a military deployment and a new State Department travel advisory.
story: Fox News correspondent Stephanie Bennett reports on the political repercussions of migrants storming the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on ‘Fox Report.’

The State Department on Saturday raised its Travel Advisory for Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta to Level 3: Reconsider Travel after tens of thousands of migrants surged into the Spanish territory from neighboring Morocco, prompting a major security response.
The updated advisory warns that the "massive and uncontrolled arrival of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta may lead to unpredictable and dangerous security situations."

"Spain has deployed the Spanish military, Spanish National Police, and Guardia Civil as a result of this serious situation," the advisory states. "Americans should reconsider travel to the area given the risks posed to their safety and security."
SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD

The advisory applies only to Ceuta, an autonomous Spanish city on the northern coast of Africa that borders Morocco. The rest of Spain remains under its existing travel advisory level.Assistant Secretary of State Dylan Johnson said the advisory was updated in response to what he described as the "mass invasion of tens of thousands of illegal migrants."

"This invasion is the direct result of the Spanish government's refusal to secure its borders and defend its people — and now threatens the security of Europe," Johnson said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
TRUMP BLASTS SPAIN MIGRANT SURGE AS 'CATASTROPHE,' WARNS US COULD FACE WORSE IF DEMOCRATS REGAIN POWER
A map shows Ceuta, a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast bordering Morocco. (Fox News)
"The United States stands with the Spanish people and all European peoples in defense of their sovereignty."

Johnson added that the U.S. welcomes efforts by Spain, Morocco and European partners to "reestablish control of the border, repel illegal migrants, prevent further loss of life, and remove those illegally in Europe."

Spanish officials have scrambled to respond after tens of thousands of migrants crossed into Ceuta this week. Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas said Friday that about 60,000 migrants entered the enclave over a 24-hour period, while Spain's Interior Ministry later estimated roughly 50,000 arrivals since Thursday. Authorities said thousands have since returned to Morocco.
SOCIALIST SPANISH PM BLASTS MELONI OVER RESTORED BORDER CONTROLS AFTER CEUTA SURGE, DEMANDS EMERGENCY MEETING

Migrants cross on foot into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco by attempting to swim, according to Spain's Guardia Civil, near the border with Ceuta, in Fnideq, Morocco, July 30, 2026, in this still image obtained by Reuters (Reuters)

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain would boost the presence of security forces in Ceuta, deploy a physical sea barrier to help facilitate repatriations and continue working with Moroccan authorities to combat human trafficking networks.

Authorities have linked the migrant surge to a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling involving migrants arriving by sea. Sánchez said human trafficking organizations misrepresented the decision, triggering the influx.
The crisis also drew comments from President Donald Trump during a Cabinet meeting Friday at Camp David.

"You know, I saw Spain yesterday, and I watched the catastrophe that took place. It looks like an invasion of a country by hundreds of thousands of people. And that same thing is going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected," Trump said.

Earlier Friday, Trump also told Fox News chief White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich: "It's terrible. Remember that picture. That's going to be us in three years if the wrong side gets in."

Ceuta, along with the Spanish enclave of Melilla, has long been a flashpoint for illegal migration into Europe because both territories sit on the African mainland while remaining part of Spain and the European Union.

title: Socialist Spanish PM blasts Meloni over restored border controls after Ceuta surge, demands emergency meeting
summary: Pedro Sánchez called Europe's response "selfish" and "unlawful" after Italy suspended Schengen Area free-travel arrangements with Spain over the crisis.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports from Ceuta, Spain, where Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has deployed military forces after a massive surge of Moroccan migrants overwhelmed border crossings and strained local resources.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez broadly blasted fellow European leaders for their response to the surge of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish border, seemingly criticizing Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni for deciding to resume European border controls in the wake of the incident.

Sánchez appeared to take issue with Italy's decision to temporarily suspend Schengen Area free-travel arrangements with Spain. The Schengen Area is an agreement between 29 European countries that abolishes passport controls and allows people to travel across European borders without providing documents.

"In the current international context, the European Union cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction," Sánchez said in a letter obtained by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) newswire.
Sánchez, who leads the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, touted his country's quick turnaround in expelling nearly all of the 50,000-60,000 migrants who crossed the border back to Morocco.

"Despite these indisputable facts," Sánchez wrote, "the reaction of European governments over the past few hours has been rather asymmetric. Most have showed us their support and solidarity, and have offered their assistance. Others, however, have chosen to attack Spain and to call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen Area.
MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

"Such an attitude — driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest — is not only contrary to European law, humanitarian law, and the principles of solidarity that bind us together," he reportedly wrote.

"It is also contrary to Europe’s long-term interests and to the most basic common sense, because Ceuta is not part of the Schengen Area, because there are almost no irregular migrants left unreturned, and because Spain is, according to Frontex, one of the least porous external borders of the European Union, with a number of irregular entries that is half that recorded, for example, in Italy in recent years (2021–2026)."

Sánchez additionally requested a formal meeting of the interior ministers of all 27 European Union countries in the letter, which was addressed to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa and Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin.
Ireland is serving its one-year term as the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union.

Sánchez's request followed a mass stampede of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, which shares a land border with Morocco in North Africa. Approximately 50,000 to 60,000 people illegally rushed over the border into European territory, according to Spanish local and national authorities.
Tens of Thousands of Migrants Enter Spanish Territory ( )
The shocking footage of the flood of people prompted a worldwide response, including from President Donald Trump.
Meloni, a conservative, announced the signing of a letter by 22 EU countries calling for stronger borders.
"The images arriving from Ceuta have once again demonstrated how urgent it is for Europe to respond to illegal immigration," Meloni wrote Saturday in a post on X.

"This is why Italy has promoted, together with Denmark, a letter signed by 22 EU member states, which calls for joint action to strengthen external borders, combat irregular immigration, fight human traffickers, make returns more effective, and eliminate any factor that could incentivize new illegal entries," Meloni added.

"It is an important signal: the line that Italy has long supported is today shared by an ever-growing number of European nation. Defending the external borders of the Union is not the interest of a single Nation. It is a shared responsibility of Europe."

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni speaks at the conclusion of Italian-German government consultations in Rome Jan. 23, 2026. Meloni on Saturday announced a joint letter singed by 23 European nations demanding stronger European border protections. (Remo Casilli/Reuters)

Irish Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan, as part of Ireland's EU presidency, will convene a meeting of the EU's Justice and Home Affairs Council to respond to the crisis, Martin announced in a post on X Saturday.

Ceuta's President, Juan Jesús Vivas, said at least 60,000 people — about 70% of the territory's population — crossed over from Morocco. Spain's interior ministry released its own figures shortly after Vivas spoke Friday, estimating that some 50,000 people had crossed from Morocco since Thursday. It added that 48,300 had already returned to Morocco by Friday evening, with hundreds more going back by the hour.
Von der Leyen claimed none of the migrants who crossed into Ceuta made it to the European mainland and that virtually all of them had returned to Morocco.

At least 67 people were killed in the border rush. As a result, Spain announced it was installing a 500-meter barrier in the sea to combat future migration pushes.

title: Trump-backed John James wins Michigan’s GOP primary for governor
summary: Rep. John James has won Michigan’s Republican nomination for governor, NBC News projects.
story: Rep. John James has won Michigan’s Republican nomination for governor, NBC News projects.
James, who represents the Detroit suburbs, prevailed in the primary despite being vastly outspent by his opponent, wealthy businessman Perry Johnson.

President Donald Trump, despite harboring early concerns that a bid for higher office would put the two-term congressman’s competitive House district at risk, endorsed James and last week traveled to the state to campaign for him.

James, 45, will face Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, the winner of Tuesday’s Democratic primary, this fall in one of the most fiercely contested battleground states. Term limits prevent Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, a Democrat, from seeking re-election.

An Army veteran who lost two Senate races before winning his House seat in 2022, James presented himself throughout the race as a capable public servant with applicable business experience, given his work with his family’s logistics company.

“This is an amazing state with all the great ingredients, but for the past seven-and-a-half years, under Gretchen Whitmer, we’ve been led to higher taxes, more crime on the roads — and frankly, the roads we have aren’t fixed yet,” James said during a televised debate last month, throwing back to Whitmer’s 2018 campaign vow to “fix the damn roads.”

“We’re going to work together to make sure that our children can read, to make sure that we put criminals in jail, and we hold those accountable who continue to let them back out,” James added. “And we’re going to be making sure that we come together to accomplish the mission of increasing hope and purpose with tested, positive leadership that has actually been tested from the battlefield to business to delivering for you right now.”

Johnson, 78, pounded the state with more than $31 million worth of ads, according to AdImpact, an ad-tracking firm. He drew on his work in quality control and improving business efficiencies while campaigning on a plan to eliminate the state’s income tax. Johnson also drew on his personal wealth, self-funding his run while declining political donations.
“In the state of Michigan, people are really tired of the politicians,” Johnson told NBC News in an interview last month. “I am an outsider. Nobody denies this fact. I’m the outsider of outsiders.”
James’ campaign spent a fraction on advertising — $2.8 million, according to AdImpact.

One potential factor in the results was the absence of former state Attorney General Mike Cox, who dropped out of the primary on July 17 and threw his support to James. Several polls had shown Cox grabbing a substantial share of the Republican vote and raised the possibility of an unpredictable three-way split that could have benefited Johnson.

Meanwhile, the general election challenge eased a bit for Democrats in May when former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan ended his independent bid for governor. Duggan, a longtime Democrat, had expressed disappointment with both major political parties but caught attention — and grief — from Democrats who noted his reluctance to aggressively criticize Trump.
Michigan voters have not elected a Democrat to succeed a Democrat as governor in more than 65 years.
Benson deputy campaign manager Alyssa Bradley wrote in an email that the secretary of state “begins the general election with something no other candidate can claim: a record of delivering.”
An accompanying campaign memo took a parting shot at both Republican candidates for governor.

“John James and Perry Johnson spent this year lobbing personal attacks at each other and competing for Donald Trump’s attention, not talking to Michigan families about the cost of housing, healthcare, or keeping the lights on,” the memo read. “Both Republican candidates focused on election denying and Donald Trump, while Jocelyn has stayed focused on the issues affecting Michigan families every day.”

title: Senators vote to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress for pleading the Fifth
summary: Fauci declined to answer senators’ questions over 100 times during last week’s hearing, angering Republican lawmakers who have targeted him for years.
story: Senate Republicans voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he declined to answer lawmakers’ questions during a fiery hearing last week.

Fauci, who has been a target of the right since he served as a top health official during the Covid pandemic, repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment right during the hearing, explaining in his opening remarks that he believed Republicans would try to use his testimony to prosecute him.
Now, Republicans on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee have pushed to do just that with the 8-5, party-line vote.

“We are voting on whether a witness who has received the benefit of a sweeping federal pardon can be ordered by this committee to answer questions and then defy that order without consequence,” committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., said in his opening statement at the meeting. Paul was referring to a pardon that then-President Joe Biden gave to Fauci and several others just prior to leaving office, which Biden said was to protect them from potential politically motivated prosecutions.

The committee can refer the contempt of Congress resolution directly to the Justice Department or request that Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., hold a full Senate vote. Paul said yesterday that the “first thing we will do” if the resolution was approved would be to refer the matter to the Justice Department.

If Paul did ask the full Senate to vote on the resolution, it probably would not have enough support to clear the 60-vote threshold that would be needed for the measure to pass in the narrowly divided chamber.

If Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, chooses to try to prosecute the case, her office would need to secure an indictment from a grand jury in the district, where she has a mixed track record.
In a statement, Fauci’s lawyer called the vote “a crude political stunt intended to punish Dr. Fauci for exercising his constitutional rights.”

“Today’s resolution is a continuation of Senator Paul’s personal vendetta against Dr. Fauci, who spent 50 years in public health and has saved countless lives,” the lawyer, David Schertler, said. “It is shameful and wrong that Senator Paul is abusing his power by trying to weaponize the Justice Department against an honorable public servant.”

Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., said in his opening remarks at the meeting that the committee vote would create a “damaging precedent” that would cause future congressional witnesses to resist providing congressional testimony.

“If this committee now seeks to punish a witness for asserting their constitutional protected Fifth Amendment rights, future witnesses will argue that appearing before Congress exposes them to punishment, regardless of whether they comply with the subpoena and invoke a constitutional protection,” said Peters, the top Democrat on the committee.
“They will point directly to this vote, this vote, as a justification for refusing to appear at all,” Peters said.
As the meeting progressed, Democrats called for votes to table the contempt resolution five times — a push that was rejected along party lines.
Paul has argued that Fauci, the former head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, could not invoke the Fifth Amendment right because of his pre-emptive pardon from Biden.

“I ordered him to answer and warned him about contempt, yet he still refused,” Paul said in a statement Tuesday. “That is obstruction of a congressional investigation. The Committee will act accordingly.”

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said in remarks before the committee vote that his investigation of Fauci has “just begun.” Johnson’s office announced yesterday that the subcommittee he leads has obtained a copy of Fauci’s iPhone. Fauci used the phone when serving in the Department of Health and Human Services during the pandemic.

“We’ve invited Dr. Fauci for a transcribed interview,” Johnson said. “OK, he doesn’t want to do it in front of the American public. Come in front of our committee. You say you you have nothing to hide. Good. We’ll do it behind closed doors. We’ll transcribe it. That that’s only one of the interviews we’ll be conducting.”

Republicans also argued in pressing for the contempt resolution that Fauci effectively “waived” his Fifth Amendment right by delivering “his opening testimony on subject matter pertinent to the questions under inquiry.”
Abbe Smith, a Georgetown Law professor, said Republicans’ claims about Fauci’s inability to plead the Fifth did not seem correct.

“There would have to be some sort of legal understanding about the nature of the pardon and whether it is limitless, and those pre-emptive pardons, those are unique,” she said. “I’m not sure anybody knows how much protection they provide.”
Smith said she, too, would have advised Fauci to assert the Fifth if had she been his defense counsel.

Smith said Republicans’ argument that Fauci’s opening statement meant he waived his Fifth Amendment right was “a little more interesting, but ultimately specious in my view,” because Fauci used his opening statement to point to his public service, belief in accountability and previous congressional testimony while explaining that “this is a bridge too far.”
“I don’t think that sort of an opening statement is a waiver,” she said. “It’s not like he was answering specific allegations and then shutting down questioning.”

Thursday’s vote is the latest salvo in Republicans’ campaign against Fauci, which has been building for years in the wake of anti-lockdown sentiment and fierce debate over the origins of the virus. Paul has targeted Fauci for years, clashing with the doctor in previous congressional hearings and repeatedly accusing him of lying, which Fauci has denied.

On Tuesday, Paul accused Fauci of committing felonies, alleging again that the doctor lied to Congress and destroyed records. Asked in an interview on MS NOW whether he believes Fauci should go to prison, Paul said it was “a good question.”

“Did he lie to Congress?” Paul asked. “I think he did lie to Congress, and I think to be fair, that people who lie to Congress should be charged with a felony, and if convicted, go to jail. There’s also the question of destroying records. That’s also a felony crime. So I think both destroying records and lying to Congress are serious crimes.”

Fauci and his lawyers have rejected Paul’s repeated claims. In a statement last week, Schertler, Fauci’s lawyer, said that Paul’s “public crusade against Dr. Fauci can only be described as an obsessive vendetta.”
During last week’s hearing, Republicans repeatedly attacked Fauci over his leadership during the pandemic. Democrats defended Fauci and criticized the premise of the hearing as a fishing expedition.

“Given Sen. Paul’s obvious obsession with calling for my prosecution, his repeated slanderous comments about me, and recently his publicly releasing my unredacted personal diary aimed at embarrassing and intimidating me, the only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, ‘behind bars,’ unquote,” Fauci said.

title: Firefighters are working 16-hour shifts as they battle the Spokane Complex Fire
summary: The Old Trails and Autumn Lane fires were each 13% contained Wednesday, and the Fairview fire was 5% contained, according to fire officials.
story: SPOKANE, Wash. — Hundreds of firefighters are working long shifts to slow the Spokane Complex Fire ahead of hotter and drier conditions this weekend.
More than 1,500 firefighters from two dozen states are battling the conflagration, which has damaged or destroyed nearly 850 structures since it ignited Saturday.
Temperatures were expected to climb from the 80s the last two days into the upper 90s later this week with no rain on the horizon.
Still, “tremendous progress” has been made, said Tom Stokesberry, spokesman for the California Interagency Incident Management Team that is coordinating the multiagency response.

The fire has grown by only 2 acres since Monday, and fire lines are being established on the three fires that make up the Spokane Complex. About 67,000 people have been displaced, officials said, adding that the number could climb.
No deaths have been reported.
“If our lines hold through the weekend, I think we’re going to be on the path to not having this fire move anymore,” he said. “But it’s still going to be a long recovery phase.”
The Old Trails and Autumn Lane fires were each 13% contained Wednesday, and the Fairview Fire was 5% contained, according to fire officials. The fires had burned 10,546 acres by Wednesday evening.

Firefighters are embroiled in what Stokesberry called a “search and destroy” mission. Elite Hotshot crews are stationed within acres of one another in an effort to mitigate all hot spots as they emerge, he said.

The crews are sleeping just five to seven hours a night, and they are working 16-hour shifts. Their deployments are typically two weeks before they are replaced by fresh crews, Stokesberry said. Additional support is expected to arrive this weekend.
“It’s trying on them, but they’re here for the long haul,” he said.

Michael Kelly, a spokesperson for the Washington State Department of Natural Resources, said that with more than 800 structures lost, the fire is “likely one of the most destructive in state history.”
The 2023 Grey and Oregon Road fires outside Spokane destroyed 350 structures, Kelly said.
Progress was thwarted this week when 40 drones entered restricted airspace and forced aerial crews to land until flight paths were cleared, Stokesberry said.
“If you fly, we can’t,” he said. “It puts crews at risk. It puts life and property at risk, the infrastructure at risk. It puts everything at risk.”

Drones have interrupted firefighters in the past, including in the Palisades Fire last year. A Southern California man was charged with recklessly operating a drone that crashed into a Super Scooper firefighting aircraft. He pleaded guilty, the U.S. Justice Department said.

It was not immediately clear whether any drone operators have been identified or questioned in connection with the recent incidents. Stokesberry said the skies have remained free of uncrewed aircraft since Monday, which has allowed fire crews to attack from above and below.
A man suspected of arson in one of the fires is expected to be arraigned Thursday.

Aaron Farinacci, 37, who is accused of starting the Old Trails Fire, was charged Monday with first-degree arson. An attorney for Farinacci did not immediately respond to a request for comment after normal business hours Wednesday.
People also started the two other fires, investigators have said, though not necessarily intentionally. The exact causes remain under investigation, officials said. No one else has been arrested.
On Saturday, Paul Child, 64, was driving along railroad tracks in his rural neighborhood northwest of Spokane, he told The Associated Press. He saw a man standing and looking toward nearby trees.
“He was bent over in the brush, acting nervous,” Child said. “You get the feeling this guy’s up to something.”
After they got home, his daughter told him there was a fire, he said.

She called 911 with a description of the man. A responding sheriff’s deputy saw a man matching the description and detained him, according to court records related to Farinacci’s arrest. Officials said the man, identified as Farinacci, was released because a cause had not yet been determined, but he was later arrested and charged.
Alicia Victoria Lozano reported from Los Angeles and Morgan Chesky from Spokane.

title: Millions of eggs have been recalled due to Salmonella contamination — here’s how to stay safe
summary: A multistate salmonella outbreak linked to eggs has sickened nearly one hundred people. Learn the symptoms, risks, and simple steps to protect your family from infection.
story: A multistate salmonella outbreak tied to eggs is currently under investigation by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), with 98 illnesses and 26 hospitalizations reported across 17 states so far. The source has been traced to a Texas egg producer, and a recall is already in effect — but for many households, the eggs in question may still be sitting in the fridge.
Keep reading for everything you need to know, including more details about the outbreak and the practical steps you can take right now to protect yourself and your family.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What is salmonella and how do you get it?

Salmonella refers to a group of bacteria that cause an illness known as salmonellosis (commonly referred to as simply salmonella). People typically become infected after swallowing the bacteria, which live in the intestines of both people and animals. According to the CDC, that exposure can happen in more ways than most people realize: through contaminated food, by drinking contaminated water, and by touching animals, animal waste or the environments animals live in. That said, the CDC reports that contaminated food is behind most cases in the United States — including the recent outbreak, which has been linked to eggs.

While thousands of Salmonella types exist, only a small fraction are responsible for the vast majority of human illness. Warmer weather and unrefrigerated food create ideal conditions for the bacteria to grow, which is why the CDC says infections tend to climb in the summer months. It’s also worth noting that officially confirmed case counts, like the ones tied to this outbreak, likely understate the real scope: CDC estimates that only one in every 30 salmonella infections is ever diagnosed, largely because many people think they have food poisoning and just deal with it at home.
What you need to know about the most recent salmonella outbreak

Public health officials in several states are currently investigating a multistate outbreak of salmonella infections linked to eggs, with 98 cases reported and 26 hospitalizations across 17 states so far (no deaths have been reported). The source has been traced to Midwest Poultry Services, L.P., a Texas producer that recalled more than 1.5 million dozen eggs after testing raised concerns about possible contamination.

The recalled cartons — sold under brand names including Kroger, Simple Truth, Brookshire’s, Cal-Maine, and Country Morning — were distributed to stores and foodservice outlets across Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Mississippi, and New Mexico. Impacted cartons were sold in bulk and retail sizes of 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, and 60 eggs. The “best by” dates are between July 20 and August 17, 2026 and the cartons have codes P-1950 or 0840962 on them, according to the CDC.

If you have eggs matching that description in your fridge, the guidance is simple: throw them out or return them, and wash any surfaces or items that may have come into contact with them using hot, soapy water or a dishwasher.
It’s worth noting that Chipotle has separately pulled jalapeños from restaurants nationwide amid a possible link to a salmonella outbreak that has made more than 100 people sick in Minnesota.
How to protect yourself from getting salmonella
There is a lot you can do at home to lower your risk of getting salmonella. According to the CDC, these are the best steps you can take:

Refrigerate items promptly: Don’t let eggs, chicken or leftovers sit out, especially in warm weather when bacteria multiply quickly.Cook eggs and chicken thoroughly. Eggs and chicken need to reach an internal temperature of 165 degrees Fahrenheit to kill off the Salmonella bacteria. You can use a food thermometer to check the temperature of your poultry if you’re not sure if it’s thoroughly cooked.Wash your hands. Use soap and water after handling raw eggs, poultry or produce, and before eating or preparing food to help prevent transferring bacteria. Sanitize surfaces. Use disinfectant on countertops, refrigerator shelves or other items that touch raw eggs or meat. The CDC says that you can create your own disinfectant by mixing one teaspoon of liquid chlorine bleach per quart of clean water. If bleach is not your preferred disinfectant, there are plenty of products available that will sanitize surfaces without it (see below)Check for recalls. Keep an eye on NBC Selected for more recall announcements, and toss or return any product that matches a recall notice. Wash your produce. It is a good idea to rinse items like jalapeños and other fresh vegetables before eating, even if you plan to cook them.

The best products for reducing the risk of salmonella

When it comes to preventing salmonella, health officials at the CDC say the best thing you can do is practice safe food handling and use the tips above. These tools can also help keep your kitchen clean and ensure your food is cooked properly.
Lysol Pro Kitchen Antibacterial All-Purpose Cleaning Spray

Lysol Pro Kitchen Antibacterial Spray cuts through grease while killing 99.9% of bacteria on contact, including Salmonella, according to the brand. It’s formulated for kitchen surfaces, making it effective for wiping down countertops and fridge shelves after handling recalled eggs or other potentially contaminated groceries — helping prevent cross-contamination during outbreaks like this one.
TempPro TempSwift Digital Thermometer

This digital food thermometer delivers accurate readings in seconds, taking the guesswork out of cooking. Simply insert the probe into eggs, poultry, or meat to confirm they’ve reached a safe internal temperature — typically 165 degrees Fahrenheit — which effectively kills Salmonella bacteria in food.
iDesign Clear Plastic Egg Holder

The iDesign Clear Plastic Egg Holder keeps eggs organized and contained in their own space, separate from other foods. Whether you transfer eggs here or keep them in their original carton, containment helps prevent contact with other items, thus reducing the risk of cross-contamination in your fridge.
Frequently asked questions

Most people infected with salmonella develop diarrhea, fever, and stomach cramps. Some people — especially children younger than 5 years old, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems — may develop a more severe illness requiring medical treatment or hospitalization.

According to the Cleveland Clinic, you should call your healthcare provider right away if you have diarrhea with a fever greater than 102 degrees Fahrenheit, diarrhea lasting more than two days without improvement, bloody diarrhea, vomiting so severe you can’t keep liquids down or signs of dehydration like reduced urination, a dry mouth and throat, or dizziness when standing. Left untreated, severe cases can lead to dehydration or the infection spreading beyond the intestines, so it’s better to check in with a doctor early than to wait it out.

Symptoms typically appear 12 to 72 hours after exposure and last four to seven days, with most people recovering without any specific treatment, according to the Mayo Clinic. Diarrhea can persist for several days and, in some cases, lead to severe dehydration, particularly in young children and older adults, and it may take several months before bowel habits fully return to normal. Even after symptoms clear up, the bacteria can still be present in a person’s stool for several weeks, which is why continued handwashing matters even once you’re feeling better.

How I picked the best rolling backpacks

According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, a student’s backpack should not exceed 15 percent of their body weight due to concerns of discomfort and risk of injury to muscles and joints. “Our backs house some of the strongest muscles in our body. But add food, schoolbooks, electronics and an assortment of other items, and the weight can add up quickly,” says Shai Karpf, the owner and directing physician at North Broward Chiropractic & Wellness.

What to consider when shopping for rolling backpacks
When shopping for a rolling backpack to avoid back pain, experts recommend taking these following factors into consideration:

Size and storage: Rolling backpacks should offer a main compartment and multiple pockets to help kids store their school supplies, water bottles and smaller essentials like keys, pencils and more.Comfort: Our experts say that rolling backpacks might be hard to take up and down the stairs or on uneven surfaces, so consider a multifunctional option that can be rolled and worn on the shoulders. Also, look for padded shoulder straps, padded backs, a grip handle for comfort and an adjustable handle that can conform to your one’s size and height (though keep in mind the manufacturer’s age recommendations).Durability: Look for backpacks made from durable, water-resistant fabrics like polyester, canvas and nylon. Frequently asked questions

Heavy backpacks are all too common, and they can take a toll when students carry them around for eight or more hours at school every day. Carrying a heavy backpack can put a strain on the spine and shoulders, potentially causing short-term effects like soreness and fatigue and long-term bad habits like slouching and poor posture, according to experts I spoke to.

“The back will compensate for any load applied to it for an extended period of time,” says Dr. Jill Noble, the division director of general pediatrics at the University of Michigan Health and Dr. Ingrid Ichesco, a clinical assistant professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Health in a joint email response. “There is no evidence that structural spinal deformity can result from backpack use. There is little chance a child or teen will be permanently injured by carrying a heavy backpack.”

Rolling backpacks can be a great alternative to traditional backpacks since they “put the weight on the wheels instead of on your musculoskeletal system,” says Karpf. This is helpful for children experiencing discomfort from lugging their backpacks at school every day. It can also be a good option for those who do extracurricular activities or walk home from school.

title: 3 people killed, including suspect, in North Carolina shooting
summary: Caswell County deputies responded to a call for service just before 8 a.m. at a home in Prospect Hill.
story: A shooting Wednesday at a home in North Carolina left three people dead, including the suspect, and another person injured, authorities said.
Caswell County deputies responded to a call for service just before 8 a.m. at a home on Brooks Road in Prospect Hill, the State Bureau of Investigation said in a news release.
Deputies found multiple gunshot victims. One person was taken to the hospital in an unknown condition.
The identities of the victims and suspect have not been released. Sheriff Tony Durden said at a news conference that everyone involved is an adult and belongs to the same family.
Durden said there was no evidence that the family previously reached out to the sheriff’s office.
The Caswell County Sheriff’s Office and the North Carolina State Highway Patrol immediately responded to the shooting, the SBI said in a Facebook post.
SBI crime scene investigators are on scene processing evidence and conducting interviews.
The agency said there is no threat to the general public and that the shooting was contained to the home.
“This was an isolated incident and please keep the family in your prayers,” the sheriff said.

title: Florida pastor accused of having sex with 14-year-old boy while hiding HIV diagnosis
summary: Authorities arrested 42-year-old Timothy Chaneyfield and said they fear there may be additional victims.
story: A “dope-smoking pedophile preacher” had sex with at least one underage boy and an adult man without telling them he was HIV-positive — and Florida officials said Tuesday they fear there might be additional victims.

Timothy Chaneyfield, 42, of St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven, was arrested after he got off a plane at Orlando International Airport on July 29, the Polk County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement.
The sheriff’s office alleged that Chaneyfield and a 14-year-old boy met on a dating app before Chaneyfield took their chats to Instagram, which led to three meetings for sex.
Tips from Instagram and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children led detectives to Chaneyfield, Sheriff Grady Judd told reporters Tuesday.
A 26-year-old man who also had sex with Chaneyfield was located by investigators and tested positive for HIV, Judd said.

“The 26-year-old didn’t know [Chaneyfield was HIV-positive] until we brought it to his attention, and the 14-year-old had no clue that he was having unprotected sex with an adult that was HIV-positive,” Judd said. “This guy’s nasty. He’s a menace to society, and he’s proven that.”
Polk County deputies wanted to arrest Chaneyfield last week, but he was in Baltimore, leading a funeral service.
“We actually tried to catch him while he was in Baltimore, because we didn’t even want him wandering the streets of Baltimore. What is he up to there?” Judd said.
But he said his department got “zero assistance” from authorities in Baltimore — an agency that a spokesperson for Judd identified Wednesday as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police.
A representative for the Maryland police could not immediately be reached for comment Wednesday.

Chaneyfield has been booked on suspicion of three counts of lewd battery of a minor, three counts of interfering with custody of a minor, unlawful use of a two-way communication device, three counts of traveling to meet a minor, four counts of having sex as an HIV-infected person without informing the partner, possession of marijuana and five counts of possession of drug paraphernalia.

“This is a dope-smoking preacher right here in front of you,” Judd said. “He’s a dope-smoking pedophile preacher right before you. And now he’s locked up in the county jail, where he should be. He was well-respected in the community. People trusted him; they believed in him. And now our plea is: If you’ve engaged this guy in sex, let us tell you [about his HIV status], because he didn’t.”
Chaneyfield also was the chaplain for Compassionate Care Hospice in Lakeland and had previously been employed by Crystal Lake Middle School as a substitute teacher.
“I would be shocked if there weren’t other children victims out there,” Judd said. “I would be shocked if there weren’t other victims out there. He was very active. He was very engaged.”
Calls to a publicly listed phone number for St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church on Wednesday were met with a message that the line had been disconnected.
Representatives for Compassionate Care Hospice and Broward County Public Schools could not immediately be reached for comment on Wednesday.

The United American Freewill Baptist Conference said St. James United American Free Will Baptist Church in Winter Haven “is not affiliated with, governed by, or under the ecclesiastical authority or jurisdiction of the United American Freewill Baptist Conference.”
“Accordingly, we are unable to offer guidance, insight, legal interpretation, or further comment concerning the matter,” the national body said.
It wasn’t clear Wednesday whether Chaneyfield has a criminal defense lawyer to speak on his behalf.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at https://www.rainn.org/get-help.

title: New Mexico sues DOJ and Todd Blanche, alleging they blocked Epstein probe
summary: The lawsuit was filed the day New Mexico is releasing a report of its preliminary findings from an ongoing probe into Epstein and his ranch in Stanley.
story: CEDAR CREST, N.M. — New Mexico’s attorney general sued the U.S. Justice Department on Wednesday, accusing it of blocking the state from investigating sex crimes at Jeffrey Epstein’s sprawling ranch near Santa Fe.

The lawsuit in federal court in Washington, D.C., said the department and acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stonewalled New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez’s criminal investigation into Epstein and others, taking steps that “actively harms victims and undermines the public interest.”

The lawsuit seeking judicial intervention to force the federal government to turn over materials to New Mexico’s investigators was filed the same day that the state released a report saying “those directly responsible for protecting New Mexicans relied on others to do their job,” including federal prosecutors in New York.

“The federal prosecutors, though, never prioritized New Mexicans, focusing instead on Epstein’s misdeeds in New York, Palm Beach, Florida, and the Virgin Islands, while leaving Epstein’s offenses in New Mexico unexamined,” the report said.

Meanwhile, according to the Washington lawsuit, Torrez and his senior prosecutors “have faced sustained resistance” to the kind of information-sharing that had occurred in the past between state and federal investigators.

In a statement, the Justice Department said it was not releasing some information the state requested because federal court orders ban disclosing “victim-identifying information carte blanche, and New Mexico has provided no lawful basis to justify such sweeping disclosures.”
It said protecting victim privacy remains a top priority, though the Justice Department “remains available to assist New Mexico’s investigation consistent with the law and binding court orders.”
Torrez, in an interview with NBC News’ Hallie Jackson, accused the Justice Department of hiding “behind the Epstein survivors.”
“We have provided them with ample legal justifications” for releasing the files, Torrez said.

The lawsuit said the Justice Department and Blanche were hiding information about Epstein and his co-conspirators when New Mexico is one of the few jurisdictions that may still be able to hold Epstein’s associates accountable or “provide some sense of justice to survivors.”
In a videoconference call with reporters, Torrez said his office has made 10 separate requests for key information and has been ignored or denied.
“We have heard repeatedly they will cooperate and what our team has experienced is anything but cooperation,” Torrez said.
“Todd Blanche today with a stroke of a pen could grant us the access that he claimed,” Torrez said. “Instead they have decided to stonewall, to obstruct and to frankly conceal for whatever reason.”
The lawsuit references a Justice Department prosecution memo that describes a sexual assault at Zorro Ranch by a woman who was not Epstein’s former girlfriend and close associate, Ghislaine Maxwell.
Asked on “Hallie Jackson Now” whether Torrez believes there is another woman who facilitated assaults in a similar way to Maxwell, he said, “The truth is we don’t know at this point.”
Torrez added that having access to all the files would put them in a better position to seek the answer to that and other questions.
Epstein took his own life in a federal jail in New York City in August 2019 after he was denied bail on sex trafficking charges lodged against him when he was arrested a month earlier.

Maxwell is serving a 20-year prison sentence after she was convicted in 2021 of sex trafficking charges at a trial in Manhattan, where some of the witness testimony alleged that Epstein and Maxwell had sexually abused women at the New Mexico ranch.

Epstein purchased his sprawling estate, Zorro Ranch, in Stanley, New Mexico, a sparsely populated ranching community about 30 miles south of Santa Fe, in 1993 from former Democratic Gov. Bruce King and built a hilltop mansion with a private airstrip and helipad.

The property was sold by Epstein’s estate in 2023 to the family of Don Huffines, a Republican who was recently appointed state comptroller in Texas. In a February social media post on X, Huffines said the property has been renamed San Rafael Ranch after a saint associated with healing and that his family plans to operate a Christian retreat there.
In December, the Justice Department started releasing investigative records pertaining to Epstein and Maxwell in accordance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

Complaints quickly arose about shoddy redactions and too many sealed materials from accusers and members of Congress who fought to pass the transparency act. Records that were released, including photographs, interview transcripts, call logs, court records and other documents, were either already public or heavily blacked out, and many lacked necessary context.
In a joint statement Wednesday to NBC News, some of the survivors of Epstein’s abuse said they stood behind Torrez’s request for the files.

“The DOJ’s argument that it won’t hand over files in order to protect survivors’ identities is laughable, when the DOJ has already revealed their names and personal information,” the statement said. “By holding onto these files, Todd Blanche’s DOJ is simply continuing to protect abusers.”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at https://www.rainn.org/get-help.

title: Presidential prospect Glenn Youngkin launches group focused on education policy
summary: The former governor of Virginia is targeting several battleground states with an ad campaign promoting President Donald Trump’s federal school choice program.
story: Former Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin, a Republican seen as a potential presidential candidate in 2028, has founded a national policy group that will launch with a push to promote a new school choice program.

Empowering America’s Parents will begin a multimillion-dollar advertising blitz targeting several battleground states, including Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, a person familiar with the internal planning told NBC News.

The states, led by Democratic governors, are among those that have yet to opt in to the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which was in last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill signed into law by President Donald Trump. The federal initiative is intended to expand school choices for K-12 students and their families.

“Regrettably, 20 states have refused to opt-in to these scholarships,” Youngkin said in a statement announcing the launch of his policy group and an accompanying media campaign. “Empowering America’s Parents will recognize the strong leaders who embraced this program and aggressively call out far-left governors who won’t stand with parents and are instead playing politics.”
Critics have long worried that such programs benefit private schools at the expense of public schools.

Youngkin’s move is likely to intensify speculation that he will seek the Republican nomination for president in 2028. Asked whether the group could be a vehicle for any national political ambitions that Youngkin may harbor and want to hone, the person familiar with the planning noted that Youngkin does not appear in the launch video.
“It’s a great issue for the governor,” this person added. “It’s a great accomplishment for the president.”

The group’s internal polling suggests that people express support for the tax credit once they learn about it but also that awareness of the program is low, the person familiar with the plans said. The campaign will be geared toward persuadable voters, primarily in the suburbs. Empowering America’s Parents also plans to focus on transparency in public education.

“Nothing is more important than our kids, so who’d be against scholarships for tuition, tutoring, services for kids with disabilities, all paid for by a federal tax credit with no state dollars?” a narrator says in the 30-second launch video. “Not hardworking parents — but far-left governors won’t play ball.”

Parents’ rights — particularly in education — became a core issue for Youngkin in his successful 2021 run for governor. He attacked his Democratic opponent, former Gov. Terry McAuliffe, for vetoing bills that would have allowed parents to opt their children out of lessons involving books deemed to have sexually explicit content. (The book at the center of that debate was “Beloved,” Toni Morrison’s Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about the horrors of slavery.)
A unique state law prohibits Virginia governors from serving consecutive terms. Youngkin left office this year, and questions about his White House prospects have followed him.

Vice President JD Vance leads most early polls testing a potential GOP field in 2028, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis among other possible candidates.

title: Al Roker Comes Face-to-Face with His ‘Twin’ on the TODAY Plaza: ‘That’s Freaky’
summary: Al Roker had to do a double take when he came face to face with his doppelgänger this morning.
story: Al Roker had to do a double take when he came face to face with his doppelgänger this morning.

The moment occurred Aug. 6 while the TODAY weatherman was visiting with fans on the TODAY Plaza. As he was doing a live segment, Al paused to speak with one special couple who brought a sign that caught his eye.
“I feel badly for this woman over here because it said she’s married to Al Roker’s twin,” Al said as he walked over to the couple, Shirley and Percy.
On their sign, the couple included a photo of themselves alongside Al with the text, “I’m married to Al Roker’s twin.”
They weren’t lying. Wearing a baseball cap and glasses, Percy resembles the beloved meteorologist so much, Al himself called it “freaky.”
Speaking to the couple on-air, Al self-deprecatingly joked, “How horrible is that?” while referencing Shirley’s sign.
Shirley laughed and said, “It’s not bad.”
Al was curious if people ever tell Percy he resembles the TODAY weatherman.
“A lot of people,” Percy said.
Before continuing with his scheduled weather segment, Al said, “OK, well listen, I hope it’s been as wonderful as it appears to be.”
“Wow, that’s freaky,” Al added as he walked to join his co-hosts.

Other members of the TODAY team have reflected on their own potential doppelgängers. Former co-anchor and “Making Space” host Hoda Kotb has long said she often gets mistaken for fellow broadcast journalist Gayle King. Meanwhile Saturday TODAY’s Laura Jarrett has said people name Meghan Markle among her look-alikes.

title: Role Model Surprises TODAY by Crashing Al Roker’s Weather Segment
summary: Role Model crashed Al Roker’s weather segment during an appearance on TODAY on August 6 ahead of the release of his third album.
story: Al Roker got a little help reporting the weather from a special guest this morning.
Role Model stopped by Studio 1A to lend a hand to the TODAY weatherman and give a look at the forecast across the country for Aug. 6.
To celebrate the release of the singer’s third album “Chuck Timely & The Hourglass,” which is out on Aug. 7, Al selected some special cities to highlight on the weather map.
In a play on the album title, the duo put a spotlight on the forecast in Charles City, Iowa. They also paid tribute to Role Model’s song “Joy” by highlighting the weather in Joy, Texas.
“Just like the song, it’s going to be very hot, very spicy (in Joy, Texas),” the singer said.
Moving through the map, Al and Role Model made a reference to the singer’s hit “Chasing Midnight” as they made their way to the forecast for Midnight, Mississippi.
The musician’s song “Love I You” inspired one other city on the map — Love, Arizona — as did the song “Honeydew,” which got some love with the addition of Honeydew, California on the map.
Last, but certainly not least, Al added Harmony, Maine to the map in a nod to Role Model’s song “Harmony” and his home state of Maine, which he called his “favorite area” of the map.
This isn’t the first time Al and Role Model have teamed up on air. In 2025, they collaborated for a showstopping moment during the singer’s Citi Concert Series performance.
Role Model, whose real name is Tucker Pillsbury, performed his hit “Sally, When the Wine Runs Out.”
During the song, which has become a staple at Role Model’s concerts, the singer typically invites a fan to dance with him on stage and calls them “Sally.”

Al was happy to volunteer for the assignment during the Citi Concert series and hit the stage wearing a cowboy hat and holding a wine glass. The duo left fans grinning as they sang and danced together.

Role Model has had a plethora of fans volunteer to be “Sally” during his concerts. But as he was sharing the Aug. 6 forecast with the singer, Al was curious to know if one of them stands out more than the others.
“You were my favorite,” Role Model said.

title: Alison Espach Shares if She’d Ever Write a ‘Wedding People’ Sequel
summary: Alison Espach shares if she’d ever write a Wedding People sequel amid the book being a bestselling hit after two years of publication.
story: Alison Espach’s novel “The Wedding People” was a bestselling hit, a BookTok craze and a Read With Jenna pick.

“It’s about where we are when we’re in the middle of our life and expectations versus reality. It’s about love and friendship and finding that love when you least expect it,” Jenna Bush Hager said when the book first came out.
“I think you will love this book if you want to laugh, maybe shed a couple tears, but also just have a lot of fun.”
The novel covers difficult topics such as suicide and grief, but also incorporates comedy and unexpected connections. Since its debut in July 2024, the book has sold over 1.5 million copies.
When Espach joined Jenna for the Aug. 6 episode of her “Open Book With Jenna” podcast, the TODAY host asked a question top of mind for many “Wedding People” fans: “Will there ever be a sequel?”
And Espach didn’t say no.
“It’s funny, it never occurred to me to write a sequel until people started asking, and then I was like, ‘Oh, I could see that,’ so I’m not saying no,” the author told Jenna.
“I’m not going to take that as a yes, either,” Jenna wearily responded.
“Oh, it’s definitely like, ‘Who knows,’” Espach agreed. But, she added, it’s the “only book” where she hasn’t felt “entirely” sick of the characters by the end of writing it.
To her, that’s a good sign.

“By the time you publish a book, you’re usually sick of it, and you have to relearn to love it again. And I sort of missed (’The Wedding People’ characters) when I was done,” she said. “I don’t feel sick of them.”
But, she added, if a sequel does arrive, “It’ll be a while.”
“I’ll probably write the sequel when no one cares anymore,” she joked. Pretending to be her readers on release day, she added, “‘We’ve moved on, it’s been 35 years.’”

title: ‘My Life With the Walter Boys’ Season 2 Recap: 7 Things to Remember Before Season 3
summary: Here’s what to remember before My Life with the Walter Boys returns for Season 3. Read a recap of Season 2.
story: The second season of “My Life with the Walter Boys” left viewers with two major cliffhangers. After a long year of waiting, fans are about to get the answers they’ve been craving when the hit Netflix series returns for Season 3 on Aug. 6.

Will Jackie (Nikki Rodriguez) and Alex (Ashby Gentry) be able to mend their relationship after she declared her love for Cole (Noah LaLonde)? Is George (Marc Blucas) going to survive his medical emergency? Viewers are ready to devour the 10 new episodes to find out.
Before Season 3 premieres, we’re recapping all the highlights from Season 2 so you can dive right in.
Jackie Returned to Colorado After Spending the Summer in New York City
At the end of Season 1, Jackie surprised the Walter family by leaving Colorado and returning to New York to live with her uncle, Richard (Alex Quijano).

Season 2 picked up with Jackie wrapping up a summer internship. It was a lonely couple of months for the teen since Richard was MIA and traveling a lot. Jackie no longer felt like she belonged in New York City, so she decided to attend boarding school in Vermont.

As Jackie’s legal guardian, Katherine (Sarah Rafferty) had to sign the paperwork for Jackie’s school transfer, and she wasn’t so sure that uprooting the teen once again was the right move. Luckily, Katherine visited Jackie in New York and convinced her to return to Colorado.

Back at the Walter ranch, Jackie got a lukewarm welcome. Several of the Walter siblings were upset that she left so suddenly a few months beforehand, but she quickly won them over and life began to return to normal.
Jackie’s Love Triangle with Alex and Cole Took a Brief Pause Then Got Messier Than Ever
At the end of Season 1, Jackie was dating Alex but also had undeniable chemistry with his brother Cole. In the Season 1 finale, Jackie and Cole ended up sharing a kiss, then she left town.
When she returned to Colorado at the beginning of Season 2, Jackie warned Cole that she hadn’t told Alex about their kiss and asked Cole to give her some space.

Alex was understandably frosty with Jackie when she returned, especially since she had blindsided him when she left town. Over time, he softened up and the two rekindled their romance. Due to their complicated history, they decided it was best to hide their relationship for a while. However, Cole caught the two kissing and  confronted Jackie in the season finale.

When Cole asked why Jackie and Alex got back together after breaking up, she defended their relationship. She also reminded Cole that they agreed to be just friends when she returned to town, despite the fact that they’d kissed. Cole responded by saying he was never just friends with Jackie.

Jackie explained that she was afraid of losing control with Cole since he makes her feel free. Cole responded by declaring his love for Jackie and she reciprocated his feelings. Unfortunately, Alex heard it all and he emerged from the darkness to ask Jackie if she really loves Cole.
Alex Became a Bull Rider and Got a Bull Riding Sponsorship

Much to the dismay of Katherine, Alex found a new hobby in Season 2: bull riding. His mom was understandably concerned that the sport is quite dangerous, but she arranged for him to get lessons with a rode trainer named Blake (Natalie Sharp). All of Alex’s hard work paid off since he ended up getting a sponsorship at the end of the season.
The Walters Faced Obstacles While Developing Their Ranch Expansion Project

In Season 1, the Walters came up with a plan to make their ranch more profitable with a new guest ranch business. In Season 2, Jackie’s uncle Richard was closely involved with the project as an investor.

Despite the family’s initial excitement about the ranch expansion, things started spiraling out of control as Richard became more involved. Will (Johnny Link) seemed to be eating up Richard’s ideas, even though his own father, George, was apprehensive about changing the ranch too much.

When many members of Silver Falls expressed concerns about the impact the ranch expansion would have on the community, the project was threatened. Soon enough, George and Katherine didn’t like the direction the project was going in and they wanted to back out. Richard had invested too much money into the project at this point, however, and threatened to cut George out of the project.

When George discovered that the ranch used to have a vineyard on it, he asked his friend to get in touch with a local winery. They agreed to lease the land to make immediate income and start paying back their investors. Will wasn’t happy but Richard was willing to listen to George’s idea.
George Had a Health Emergency

In the season finale, viewers were left with a cliffhanger in the last seconds when an ambulance showed up at the Walter house. Will also arrived and said, “It’s dad,” implying that his father had a health emergency.
Nathan Cheated on Skylar and They Broke Up
Nathan (Corey Fogelmanis) and Skylar (Jaylan Evans) were happily dating, but then Zach (Carson MacCormac), Skylar’s ex, came into the picture.
Zach started flirting heavily with Nathan and the two ended up kissing at a school dance. Skylar caught them and they broke up.

Zach and Nathan started dating and Nathan learned more about Zach’s history with Skylar. As it turns out, Skylar and Zach hooked up during their sophomore year, but Zach hadn’t publicly announced that he was gay yet. Skylar wanted to date someone who was openly gay so they went their separate ways.

Zach came out eventually, but by the time he did, Nathan and Skylar were already dating. So, Zach tried his best to lure Nathan away from Skylar to get Skylar’s attention, in the hopes that Skylar would ditch Nathan.

Eventually, Nathan and Zach broke up and Zach tried to get back with Skylar, but he had no interest. In the season finale, Nathan apologized to Skylar and they declared their love for each other. However, Skylar made it clear that he could no longer trust Nathan, even if he still loves him.
Two New Couples Emerged: Danny and Erin and Dylan and Kiley

Erin (Alisha Newton) previously dated Cole, but they had a pretty complicated relationship and he didn’t treat her very well. When Cole’s twin brother Danny (Connor Stanhope) starred in the school play with Erin in Season 1, sparks started to fly. The two kept in touch over summer break and started dating in Season 2.

Cole was pretty upset when he found out that his brother was dating his ex in secret, but eventually warmed up to their relationship. Danny and Erin seemed like the perfect match, but struggled to figure out how to maintain their relationship with college approaching.

Alex’s friend Kiley (Mya Lowe) found an unexpected new love interest in football player Dylan (Kolton Stewart). They had apparent chemistry throughout the season, but finally kissed in the season finale. Alex spotted them smooching and looked upset, despite the fact that he was happy with Jackie.

title: Perez Hilton’s Family Speaks Out After Reports He Allegedly Livestreamed Self-Harm
summary: Perez Hilton’s family shared a statement after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream that was flagged in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
story: This story discusses self-harm. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.
Perez Hilton’s family is speaking out after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
Hilton is currently receiving medical care, according to the statement from the blogger’s family and team that was shared Aug. 5 on his website.

The statement comes after reports of “someone who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media” the night before, a Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office spokesperson told NBC News. The person was “safely recovered,” the sheriff’s office said. Police did not identify Hilton by name.

“Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez,” said the statement, signed “The Perez Hilton Team and Family.” “We are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers.”
The family added that their “focus right now is on his well-being.”
“We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time,” the statement said.

The livestream was posted to TikTok before the platform pulled the video. It appeared to show Hilton, covered in blood and holding a knife with signs of injuries. Concerned viewers commented on the livestream, asking for his contact information and offering to call for help.

According to a TikTok U.S. spokesperson, the social media platform’s automated moderator systems flagged the livestream within minutes. Then, the U.S. moderation team reviewed it and law enforcement was alerted.

The content violated the platform’s community guidelines, the spokesperson added. According to TikTok’s mental and behavioral health policies, the platform allows individuals to “discuss emotionally complex topics in a supportive way without increasing the risk of harm.”
“We don’t allow showing, promoting, or sharing plans for suicide or self-harm,” the guidelines say.

Footage from Hilton’s neighborhood, taken by NBC South Florida, showed multiple police vehicles in the area. Cameras from the local NBC affiliate showed paramedics transporting a man into an ambulance and driving away.
The police spokesperson said in a statement that family members of the individual that they recovered have been contacted.
“Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside,” the spokesperson said.

Hilton, who was born Mario Lavandeira, has three children — Mario III, Mia and Mayte Amor— all born via surrogacy. In a 2017 essay published on HuffPost, Hilton also mentioned that his mother lives with the family.
“Not many families are able to have that opportunity,” he wrote in the essay. “That difference makes us special and awesome, to me and us.”
In June, Hilton shared in a video that he and his family had moved back to Miami after a three-and-a-half-year-long stint in Las Vegas.
Hilton’s family and team said in their statement that they plan to share updates “as soon as we can.”
“Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support,” the statement said.

Chris Booker, who co-hosts “The Perez Hilton Podcast with Chris Booker” with the blogger, released a statement on Aug. 5 as well in response to the news. Booker said that he has only spoken “briefly” with Hilton’s family, who are struggling with getting updates themselves due to the security measures in place at the hospital. He reiterated that any official updates will appear on Hilton’s website.
“I am so profoundly sad for Perez and his family and what they’re all going through,” Booker said in the statement, shared on social media. “It’s truly unimaginable.”
Booker also said that the podcast is up in the air “as our collective focus is on his health.”
“I certainly hope to continue them with my friend when the time is right,” Booker wrote, adding that the support from fans has been “resounding.”
“He is very loved,” Booker wrote. “I can only hope that he feels it.”
Hilton’s agent Dante Rusciolelli, CEO and talent manager at Golden Arts Entertainment, also shared a statement on Aug. 5, asking the public to honor Hilton’s privacy as he receives care.
“At this time, we do not have any additional confirmed information to share regarding Perez Hilton’s condition,” the statement said.
Verified updates will come “directly from Dante Rusciolelli at Golden Artists Entertainment,” the statement said.

Hilton rose to fame in the early 2000s for his gossip blog, sounding off on celebrity drama. His commentary was often criticized as cyberbullying and labeled as “toxic.” However, Hilton attempted to turn a new leaf years later and embraced a gentler, softer version of himself.

“I’m aware of the fact there are going to be a lot of people with lingering resentment and a lot of skeptics,” he told the New York Times in a 2012 interview. “And that’s OK because I am not pretending to be perfect.”

title: Melanie C Explains Why Victoria Beckham Didn’t Attend Her Wedding
summary: Melanie “Mel C” Chisholm is addressing why her longtime friend and former Spice Girl member Victoria Beckham wasn’t present at her wedding.
story: Melanie “Mel C” Chisholm is addressing why her longtime friend and former Spice Girl member Victoria Beckham wasn’t present at her wedding.

The singer, known as Sporty Spice, married model and actor Chris Dingwall in July, sharing video of their special day with British Vogue. Chisholm also posted photos from their nuptials, as well as the wedding guests on her Instagram on Aug. 2.

Among the friends who attended the nuptials were fellow Spice Girls Geri Halliwell-Horner, Emma Bunton and Melanie “Mel B” Brown. While Chisholm thanked Beckham in her Instagram caption for designing her “beautiful dress,” the singer-turned-fashion designer was nowhere in sight.
During an interview on Australian radio station KIIS 1065, the hosts congratulated her on her wedding, before asking why Posh Spice was missing.

“So, Victoria was very disappointed to not be there. She was with David (Beckham) in New York and it was the football final, the World Cup,” she said. “She tried to get out of it. She isn’t the biggest football fan, she won’t mind me telling you. But the family were there and David had commitments being an ambassador for FIFA.”
She added that while she wasn’t in attendance, she designed her “gorgeous dress.”
“And she was messaging me on the day, and I actually saw her when I was in Ibiza. So we had a little catch up,” Chisholm added. “So yeah, we were giving her updates and sending her pictures.”

Victoria and David Beckham attended a number of FIFA World Cup matches, spotted in Los Angeles, Miami and the July 19 final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. During the final match, the couple were accompanied by their sons Cruz and Romeo Beckham.
Chisholm, meanwhile, described her wedding as “amazing” and “perfect.”
“My feet haven’t touched the ground, really, because we had a beautiful weekend with all our families and friends,” she said.

She also shared that “there were several Spice Girls songs” played during her wedding. In another separate interview with Australia’s “The Smallzy Show,” she said that she “walked back up the aisle with my husband to ‘2 Become 1,’ played by a beautiful string quartet.”
Additionally in her chat with KIIS 1065, the newlywed also addressed Halliwell-Horner wearing a white floral dress to her wedding.

Chisholm said she did have a chat with her friend “because it is her favorite color, she wears it every day ... but she did have a beautiful floral dress on and it was white. But I did have a little giggle with her about that.”

title: Andy Cohen Politely Reviews Craig’s Attempts at His ‘Real Housewives’ Tagline: ‘Good Starting Point’
summary: TODAY’s Craig Melvin attempted an updated “Real Housewives”-style tagline about himself, and Andy Cohen gave an honest review.
story: TODAY’s Craig Melvin still may not be “Real Housewives” ready.

A hallmark of the 20-year franchise are the taglines cast members say in each show’s intro. Lisa Vanderpump of “Beverly Hills” famously said, “Life isn’t all diamonds and rosé, but it should be,” while “Atlanta’s” Phaedra Parks opted for, “Only God can judge me, and he seems quite impressed.”
In 2022, the TODAY hosts put their own spin on the taglines with “The Real Anchors of TODAY,” which Craig Melvin and Bravo executive producer Andy Cohen revisited in Studio 1A on Aug. 5.
“As a journalist, I usually keep one ear to the ground, because I’m getting the other one pierced,” Craig said at the time, which Cohen gave a “so-so” rating.
Now, Craig’s craving redemption.
“It was mediocre,” he said. “I wanted to try again.”
As the franchise’s unmistakable soundtrack played in the studio, Craig gave it another shot.
“I may spill the tea, but I still keep the glass half full,” he said, a pun on the video podcast he launched in March 2026.
“That’s good ... yes,” Cohen responded.
But Craig wasn’t done.
“Growing up in the South, I was raised to mind my manners, not my business,” he said.
Cohen was less impressed.
“Alright, I’m lost,” Cohen responded with a head shake.
“You’re always honest,” Craig said, before giving it one more go.
“I’m in the business of news, but I’m never above a little drama,” he said.
“That’s a good starting place, we’ll work on that,” Cohen determined.
“I couldn’t be a real housewife,” Craig said with a laugh.
Of the three, Cohen said his favorite was Craig’s first attempt.
“It’s where you’re at on the TODAY show right now,” Cohen said.

Cohen is fittingly looking back at his own television career, celebrating the 20th anniversary of the “Real Housewives” franchise, which he’s led since it launched in 2006 with “The Real Housewives of Orange County.” To mark the milestone, Bravo will release “Real Housewives Ultimate Girls Trip: Roaring 20th,” which premieres Aug. 9.
But Cohen has no intention of slowing down.
“I want to keep this going as long as I can,” Cohen said. “I got kids to feed.”

title: Harry Jowsey Is in the ‘Best Place’ He’s Ever Been After ‘Let’s Marry Harry’
summary: Harry Jowsey speaks to TODAY.com about his new show, Let’s Marry Harry, and why he’s int he best place he’s ever been ahead of the show’s finale.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Harry Jowsey has flirted his way across the Netflix dating show universe, from his “Too Hot to Handle” debut to his “Perfect Match” antics. But in his new series, “Let’s Marry Harry,” he’s going all in to find his forever beau.
