With “Let’s Marry Harry” production behind him, Harry tells TODAY.com, “It was perfect.”
“I’m in the best place I’ve ever been,” he says.

Across the eight-episode season, the 29-year-old reality dating vet pursues 20 hopeful women, each sporting an engagement ring and vying for his hand in marriage — and the approval of his hand-picked matchmaking squad.

Jowsey’s friends Amanda Kloots, Sonny Henty and ex-girlfriend Georgia Hassarati of “Too Hot to Handle” all pulled strings behind the scenes, making calls like who gets dates, who gets cut and who gets a step closer to the altar. Executive producer and “Call Her Daddy” host Alex Cooper also joined to advise Jowsey as drama reached its boiling point.
Jowsey joined TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager and Willie Geist to discuss the show on Aug. 5, its premiere date. The final episode premieres Aug. 12.

Discussing his evolution from his reality debut to now, Jowsey said, “I feel like that guy back then didn’t really care too much about anyone else’s feelings. I was a class clown, I was going to do whatever I wanted.”
But for “Let’s Marry Harry,” he joked, he’s “figured out empathy and thoughts.”

After chatting with Jenna and Willie, Jowsey stuck around to break the rest down for TODAY.com: opening up to commitment, dating on and off screen and the self-help steps that got him ready to say “I do.”
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

After losing my dad, it was really a pivotal moment in my life. Seeing my sisters with their husbands and kids, and just knowing that I really wish I had that for my dad. Coming back to LA and not having a good support system, I was like, I’ve really got to be serious about love.
I kept asking for a sign, and they kept showing up. It was good.

Leading into it, it didn’t really cross my mind until the first day, and then I was like, “Oh my God, this is really scary.” I think the first fear, or thought throughout, I was just more upset about hurting people because I don’t want to be that guy anymore, and I don’t want to break anyone’s hearts. And obviously, it’s difficult, because that’s kind of a big thing that happens on dating shows. So I think that was my biggest fear going through the whole thing, I don’t want to break someone’s heart.

There was so much different. I was reading a bunch of self-help books, and then Amanda Kloots sat me down for four and a half hours before it, just quizzing everything about my dating life and making sure I was ready. I also knew if I didn’t take it serious and if I was playing around and being a silly sausage, it wouldn’t be good for anyone, and it would really suck. Netflix put all this like money into it and love into it, and I just wanted to make sure I was doing it as best I could.
“He’s Scared, She’s Scared.” It’s this book about self sabotage. I was trying to figure out if I do that a lot, but I think I’m all good now.

All the girls just made it such a safe space. I think I was more upset when they had to hand the rings back. I know a lot of them got quite attached to them. I was just really appreciative because they all were just so warm and made it safe.

I think so. I think dating these days is so difficult, regardless of any of the silly stuff I’ve done. But I feel like it’s helped me become just a way better version of myself because with all those lows, you know you can only come back up, and I’m just grateful I was able to learn from my mistakes.
Yeah, it was perfect. And I’m in the the best place I’ve ever been, so I’m really happy.

I realized I’ve been quite easy to be dismissive and avoidant in the past. Being in an environment like that where you just have to face everything head-on, because if you don’t, then you’re not going to get what you want to show, and also you’re not going to deal with the problem. So it really made me be way better at communicating and also dealing with 20 different personalities at once and learning about that and looking within a lot, which was quite fascinating.
I feel like more now, but leading into the show, I was like, ‘I’m cooked.’ That’s why they had to bring my friends in because I’m spiraling. But yeah, now I trust my thoughts and feelings.

I think I was more nervous for her. It’s such a brave thing to do, and to be like, OK, I’m willing to be a part of this and help an ex when we’ve had quite a colorful past together. I was really grateful that she wanted to do it.
I think “Too Hot to Handle” Harry should have never been in a relationship. He should have just had fun and lived in the moment. I feel like now it’s one person, forever locked in.

title: Will There Be a Season 2 of ‘Sterling Point?’ What Star Ella Rubin Hopes to See
summary: What happens at the end of Prime Video’s “Sterling Point”? Ella Rubin unpacks the twist and shares her Season 2 hopes.
story: In the post-“Summer I Turned Pretty” and “Off Campus” television landscape, “Sterling Point” is the latest to join the ranks of Prime Video teen dramas.

Season 1 of “Sterling Point,” which released Aug. 5, has all the key ingredients: a slow-burn love triangle, beautiful on-location setting, a trendy soundtrack and an ensemble cast of up-and-coming young actors — including leading lady Ella Rubin, who previously supported movies like “The Idea of You” and “Anora.”

“Sterling Point,” created by Megan Park, is an original series that follows city-girl Annie Jacobson after learning she has secret ties to Canada. Annie’s adoptive mother died when she was young, and her father has told her little about her mother’s family.

After her estranged grandfather’s death, Annie heads to his home on Sterling Point, an island off Lake Muskoka in Canada, giving her more questions than answers — at first — and a new outlook on what it means to grow up.
Here’s what to know about the ending of “Sterling Point,” including that plot twist within a plot twist, and what it means for a potential second season.
Warning: Spoilers from “Sterling Point” below.
What Happens in ‘Sterling Point’?
Audiences are right alongside Annie as she uncovers the lies she and her newfound extended family have been told.
After finding letters from her grandfather, previously hidden by her dad, Steven (Jay Duplass), Annie learns about her ties to Canada.

Shortly after arriving in Lake Muskoka, Annie, who was told growing up her parents couldn’t conceive, learns her mother had a biological daughter roughly two years after adopting Annie and her twin brother, Connor.

Ramona was raised by their grandfather in Canada and spent her summers on Sterling Point, which all three siblings will now inherit. Annie and Ramona go from painfully co-existing to forming a deep bond through their separate-but-shared mysterious childhoods.

Together, they learn that Annie and Ramona’s mother grew up coming to the island as a child and had an on-and-off relationship with a man named Joe (Jeffrey Dean Morgan). After adopting Annie and Connor, their mom got pregnant, though her husband Steven was said to be infertile.

It’s revealed she planned to leave Steven, stay on the island to raise Connor, Annie and baby-on-the-way Ramona, and finally be with Joe. She returned to Sterling Point to give birth to Ramona but died in labor because of a previously unknown heart condition.
But after her death, Steven took Annie and Connor back to New York City and concealed their Sterling Point lineage.

The show had one more twist. After learning about her mom and Joe’s affair, Ramona assumed Joe was her father. Then she learns Steven is colorblind, like herself. Because colorblindness is genetic, Ramona makes Steven take a paternity test, revealing he’s also her biological father.
As Annie falls more and more in love with Lake Muskoka, Ramona becomes interested in getting to know Steven.
Where Does the First Season Leave Annie and Ramona?

After a long debate, Annie and Ramona decide to switch places. Annie stays in Sterling Point, and Ramona goes to the city to get a new vantage point. In the final scene, Ramona wake up in Annie’s room in Brooklyn, and Annie in Ramona’s.
“I loved the ‘Parent Trap’-esque ending, and I thought it was that perfect kind of ambiguous, yet satisfying closing loop to the first season,” Rubin tells TODAY.com.
Will There Be a ‘Sterling Point’ Season 2?
Rubin is hoping for a second season to return as Annie.
“Sterling Point” has not been officially renewed for a second season. Park, who wrote and directed the series, has spoken about the possibility of expanding beyond an eight-episode debut.
Rubin shares what she could envision for Annie in the future.

“I don’t know what I can tease, not because it’s a secret, but because there’s so many amazing routes that Annie’s journey can take,” Rubin tells TODAY.com. “I truly don’t know what’s going to happen. And that’s both exciting and nerve-racking because, she feels like someone who’s almost become a sort of friend of mine.
“I don’t know what she’s up to right now, but I hope that she and Ramona are happy with their choices, and also that it leads to some more, you know, fun conflict,” Rubin adds with a laugh.

title: Ella Rubin Channeled These Early 2000s Ballads For Starring Role in Teen Drama ‘Sterling Point’
summary: Ella Rubin unpacks her starring role in Prime Video’s “Sterling Point” and shares how she journaled and listened to music to get into character as Annie.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

In Prime Video’s new teen drama series, “Sterling Point,” Ella Rubin’s Annie Jacobson leaves the comforts of city life for Lake Muskoka, Canada, and encounters an unexpected reunion with both old and new friends.
The same can be said for Rubin herself, who is making her debut as a leading lady.

Like Annie, Rubin is a born-and-raised New Yorker, and, like Annie, the 24-year-old went to Canada and had an “out-of-body experience,” processing what it means to grow from supporting roles in “Anora,” “The Idea of You” and the “Gossip Girl” reboot into a new phase of her career.

“Sterling Point,” created by Megan Park with executive producers Joshua Schwartz and Stephanie Savage of “Gossip Girl” and the “The O.C.,” is a twisty family mystery with an ensemble of wily, messy teens.

It opens with Rubin’s Annie and her twin brother, played by Keen Ruffalo (son of Mark Ruffalo), learning of their estranged grandfather’s death. His will reveals he left them an island, Sterling Point, located off Canada’s Lake Muskoka. (“Mom was Canadian?” Rubin’s character asks in Episode 1.)

“It kind of unravels her life in this dramatic, funny, beautiful, sad way,” Rubin said of the show while appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle Aug. 3. “She discovers a lot of secrets that were kept from her, and also a lot of secrets she kind of kept from herself.

“And of course there’s romance and sisterhood and friendship, and it’s really a fun, funny series, but also I think it doesn’t shy away from emotion and tenderness, and it’s a refreshingly tender show,” she adds.

Speaking with TODAY.com after her live interview, Rubin dives into her process finding Annie, unpacks the unscripted moments that made the final cut and pitches why “Sterling Point” stands out among today’s teen drama shows.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

There was a lot more trust, a lot more creative agency. And also just a bigger responsibility in the sense that I wanted to be a good leader in certain ways, and take the responsibilities seriously, of getting to be so lucky to be in a show like this. I just wanted to take it very seriously and kind of take all that I’d learned in the years of doing it here and there and create a fun, healthy, productive environment.

It felt so, so cool. It was really incredible wish fulfillment. They’re just legends, and so I knew I was in really great hands. And then also, five years after doing a job where I was really nervous and unsure, I just felt so lucky to be entrusted in this new way. It was just the coolest out-of-body experience. And also, they’re both really great people.
It just feels really cool to be old enough to have been doing this long enough that I can reunite with someone. It also was a trip in that sense, in the best way.

I think something really special about “Sterling Point” is the grounded-ness, and I think the brilliance of combining Josh and Steph and Megan Park is that there’s a propulsive plot, and it’s a teen drama, and it’s coming of age, but then it also has really real language. It’s very grounded. There’s a lot of genuine emotion. There’s a lot of messiness, and I think we allow the characters to be imperfect, and the show is really, really tender.

Especially with being young women in a show, allowing them to not always be perfectly likable is a really special thing. It explores really intense themes, and it balances dark and light in a beautiful way. There is a lot of grief, and there’s trauma, and then there’s also a lot of friendship and first love and romance and excitement.
Can I tell you something funny about that? That was not planned!

I think something I really, really loved about filming this show is that Megan encouraged constant improvisation, changes, sort of flowing with where the scene took us, which is a really rare gift. When moments like that happen, we just get to fully lean into it and enjoy the kind of spontaneity and ridiculousness of real life, because, like, what’s better than that?
So, essentially, the seaplane took off. That happened, and I just rocked with it and was crossing my fingers that they would use it, because I loved that moment so much.

I loved doing the boating scenes. They’re probably my favorite memories from filming. First of all, I really found a knack for boating, and I shockingly just loved it and felt really comfortable, and I was in my element randomly, even though I’m a born and bred city kid.

We would do lessons, and so once I learned how to operate these boats, they kind of just sent me out. I have a little makeup kit and mirror to do touchups on myself. And then they’d scream “Action!” from another boat, and then I get to just feel really free. It was very organic, filming those scenes, because you can’t really see a camera. You’re not really being touched. You’re just out in the open, and then also, not only that, you get to be in nature all day. You’re literally sitting in the water, breathing in the air, and feeling the trees, and it was just really, really special, and it allowed me to kind of get into Annie’s headspace of becoming, in a way, one with nature.

The needle drops of this series are awesome. I’m so glad that you felt that way as well. Journaling was a huge thing for me. I had an Annie notebook that became sort of a bible to me in ways. Music was huge for me in this process, too, and I had a very extensive Annie playlist. Some of it was music she would listen to, some of it was music I would listen to get into her character, and some of it was music that was kind of indicative of what she was experiencing, or certain songs for certain characters, dedicated to certain romance storylines, but music was probably one of my primary forms of preparation.

I love this question. The Chicks, particularly “Wide Open Spaces.” I think it’s perfectly descriptive of Annie’s experience. Funny enough, there were a lot of 2000s ballads. “I‘m With You” by Avril Lavigne made a few appearances. “I’m On Fire” by Bruce Springsteen. “Wildflowers” by Tom Petty. There was a feeling in “Sterling Point” that’s like cozy, early 2000s and kind of has that energy, and I just thought that those songs really brought me into that in a really amazing way. Oh, and “Wish That You Were Here” by Florence and The Machine was a big one for Annie’s mom.

title: Andy Cohen Reveals His New Boyfriend Has Never Seen ‘Housewives’: ‘Not 1 Frame’
summary: Andy Cohen’s boyfriend has a lot to learn about the Bravo-verse and all the “Housewives” that are part of it.
story: Andy Cohen’s boyfriend has a lot to learn about the Bravo-verse and all the “Housewives” that are part of it.
The longtime Bravo producer and “Watch What Happens Live” host shared details about his relationship with businessman Kevin Sobieski after the two went public in June.

In an Aug. 5 appearance on TODAY, Cohen came to celebrate 20 years of “Real Housewives” on Bravo and spoke with Craig Melvin about “The Real Housewives Ultimate Girls Trip: Roaring 20th,” which brings together iconic women across the franchises.
While chatting with Cohen, Craig asked what Sobieski thinks about the long-running reality shows that Cohen created.
“Is he a ‘Real Housewives’ kind of guy? Craig asked.
“Never seen it,” Cohen replied.
“Not one frame?” Craig asked.
“Yes. (He not seen one frame,” Cohen confirmed.
Still, if social media has anything to say about it, Cohen’s beau will be up to speed in no time.
“His algorithm is feeding him ‘Housewives’-related things because our phones listen to everything we say. So he’s starting to, I think, get a sense of the universe. But he has no clue,” Cohen said.
“Does that not bother you at all?” Craig asked.
“No, not at all. I love it. He loves my kids and me, and that’s what’s important,” Cohen said. “But I’ll get him there.”
During a June episode of his “Andy Cohen Live” Sirius XM podcast, Cohen shared that he’d “met the person.”
“This man is kind, and strong, and smart, and he is an adult,” Cohen said. “And he loves my children, and they love him, and I love him.”
Cohen also revealed that he met his boyfriend at a mutual friend’s July Fourth party in 2025.

“We talked all night,” he said. “I very methodically put my number in his phone. Apparently, I said to him twice that night, ‘I want to make sure this number is right. … And then he said, ‘Wow, I knew you were serious when you were really, like, serious about this number.’”
The Bravo star said he took a “slow and deliberate and methodical” approach to dating his boyfriend and introducing him to his two children, Ben and Lucy.
“It has been so easy. One year later, I still can’t believe I found him.”

title: Carson Daly Clarifies He’s Still Hosting ‘The Voice’ After Spinoff Is Announced
summary: Carson Daly has no plans to leave “The Voice,” he confirms. He is not leaving The Voice but will continue to host The Voice.
story: After 30 seasons of hosting “The Voice,” Carson Daly has no plans of walking away from the reality singing competition anytime soon.

On Aug. 4, NBC announced a spinoff version of the show, titled “The Voice: Celebrity.” Set to debut in 2027, the series will feature Keke Palmer as a host and will challenge celebrities to compete for the opportunity to become the first “Voice” celebrity champion.
After the new show was announced, some fans began to wonder if it would replace the original series, leaving many to question what that meant for Carson.
The TODAY host quickly addressed the speculation in an Instagram shared on Aug. 4, clarifying that he would remain in his hosting role as “The Voice” enters Season 31.

“‘Celeb Voice’ is a fun, NEW IDEA that features some big differences like… FAMOUS PEOPLE singing for 3 coaches to see if they have what it takes. There’s lots of new twists & turns. I have been talking about it on @todayshow for a while now. I am not the right host for it. We have a NEW amazing HOST! The triple threat queen @keke who is PERFECT for it! I’m so grateful she carved out the time in her busy career to help us out. 🙏We’re all big fans & welcome her to the family,” he wrote.
Carson continued his post, addressing the rumors that he is no longer involved with the show head-on.

“Many today have asked if I’m leaving the show. Nope. We’re gonna try out these 2 formats this fall/spring & see how it goes! Hopefully this post clears up any confusion. I am still hosting the show currently. In fact, I have hosted & produced every single second of the show since day 1, 30 seasons. 16 years,” he wrote.
Carson said he will be directly involved with “The Voice: Celebrity” “from behind the scenes” and will be producing the series.
Carson ended his post by sharing an update on the upcoming season of “The Voice,” which premieres Sept. 21.

“Meanwhile, thanks for watching any/all Voice shows & we can’t wait to see you NEXT MONTH with the ‘OG’ Voice coaches @adamlevine @kellyclarkson @queenlatifah @rileyduckman & yes, me. We’ve already shot a-lot of it & it may be our best season yet!! And please tune in SPRING 2027 for Celebrity Voice! 🎤🏆,” he wrote.
When “The Voice: Celebrity” premieres in 2027, it will feature several celebrity coaches, including Joe Jonas, Queen Latifah and Riley Green.

title: Viral TV Anchor Who Fell Asleep on Air Recounts How a Night with a Teething 8-Month-Old Led to ‘Work Nightmare’
summary: Memphis news anchor Dominique Dillon spoke to TODAY about falling asleep on air and how a night up with her 8 month old led to the moment.
story: As local morning news anchor Dominique Dillon realized she had been dozing off during a live broadcast, it felt like a bad dream.

“I opened my eyes, and it was cutting to the next shot and I was like, ‘Oh my goodness, I can’t believe this just happened to me,’” Dillon told Craig Melvin and Laura Jarrett in a TODAY exclusive on Aug. 5.
“I am mortified. I was pinching myself under the desk like, ‘This has to be a nightmare.’ Like one of those work nightmares, because this is not my life right now.”

However, the reaction to the viral clip from late July has been a dream for the FOX13 Memphis anchor. The mom of 2-year-old daughter Dakota and 8-month-old daughter Delilah said she has received an “overwhelmingly” positive reaction from viewers who can relate to a parent of young children running on fumes.

Dillon shared the backstory on TODAY about why she was so sleepy during the broadcast. The viral clip shows Dillon dozing with her eyes closed and head resting on her hands in the studio while on air with a reporter on location.
The night before the viral moment, her husband had been working a double shift at BNSF Railway while she tried to put her two girls to bed.

“I was trying to get them down to sleep at 8 o’clock, but my 8-month-old, she wasn’t having it,” Dillon said. “She was teething, and I just couldn’t console her. I gave her some teething medicine and nothing was working. The next thing you know it’s 10:30, 11 o’clock before I can get actually get her down to sleep. Then all I have is a couple hours of rest before I have to be up in the morning and be at work.”

Dillon normally wakes up at 1:30 a.m. to start preparing for her early morning anchor shift from 4:30 to 5 a.m. Working on short rest, she drifted off into a mini nap live on air before her colleague, Fox 13 meteorologist Brittani DuBose, whispered her name from across the room to try to snap her out of it.
The doze happened so quickly it even took the producers by surprise.

“They’re there, but they didn’t think I was sleeping,” Dillon said on TODAY. “They thought I was simply looking down at my tablet, because who falls asleep in one minute, sitting up, in front of cameras?”

Dillon, who welcomed her second child in December, went on to poke fun at the moment. Her colleague and FOX13 Good Morning Memphis anchor Ernie Freeman shared a selfie of himself with Dillon, who was pretending to nap.
“Now that ‘The Big Show’ is over, it’s time for Dominique Dillon to catch another nap,” he wrote on Facebook.
Dillon reposted the photo on Facebook on July 29, adding, “Couldn’t even give me a nudge. Brittani DuBose FOX13 had my back though!”
“Those morning shifts are so challenging. Let’s give her some grace and support,” one person commented on the Instagram video.

“Well we understand she has a little one at the house so her nights are different right now,” another commented on Dillon’s post, while another added, “I used to want to catch a nap at a stoplight when I was in baby mode. All mamas can relate.”
Dillon was grateful for the positive support considering how ugly the internet can get after a viral moment like that.

“It’s not always a nice place, and what I love so much about this situation is that it shows the good side of humanity and that people understand what I’m going through as a mother,” she said on TODAY. “There’s so many mothers out there and parents in general who work hard. They show up to work, they give 100% and then they go home and that’s like a whole ‘nother full-time job as well, and they’re giving 100% to their families.”
The California native started in news in 2017 and worked in Texas and Louisiana before joining the station in Memphis in 2019.
The day after her little mid-morning snooze, she shared a photo an inspirational quote on Facebook.

“‘Every morning, you have two choices: continue to sleep with your dreams or wake up and chase them,’ — Arnold Schwarzenegger. Wise words from my former Governor,” the California native wrote, adding, “Good morning!”
She wants other hard-working parents to know she is in their corner after all the support she has received.

“I just want parents to know that you’re doing a great job, and keep it up,” she said on TODAY. “And to the mothers out there, those long nights, they’re worth it. Continue to show up to work, give your best and then also come home and give your best to your children as well because all they want is for their parents to show up and be there for them.”

title: ‘The Voice’ Gets ‘Celebrity’ Spinoff With New Coaches, Host and Format
summary: “The Voice” is switching things up again!
story: “The Voice” is switching things up again!
Following Season 29’s “The Voice: Battle of Champions,” it appears the NBC singing competition is undergoing another makeover for 2027.

On Aug. 4, it was revealed that NBC has started production for “The Voice: Celebrity,” where stars ranging from actors, musicians, influencers and more will compete to become the first “Voice” celebrity champion.
“The Voice: Celebrity” will feature new and returning coaches, as well as a new host.

Before the revamped edition airs, Season 30 of “The Voice” — with returning coaches Adam Levine and Kelly Clarkson and newcomers Queen Latifah and country music singer Riley Green — will premiere on Sept. 21.
Read on to learn more about “The Voice: Celebrity,” coming in 2027.
Who Will Host ‘The Voice: Celebrity’?
Giving host Carson Daly a break for this celebrity edition is Keke Palmer. The multi-hyphenate will take the helm, bringing her charisma and energy to “The Voice” stage.
Who Are the Coaches for ‘The Voice: Celebrity’?

“The Voice: Celebrity” will have Joe Jonas making his coaching debut this season. He will be joined by Queen Latifah and Riley Green, who will be returning to their red chairs after participating in Season 30.
Who are the Celebrities Competing on ‘The Voice: Celebrity’?
The celebrities that will be part of the inaugural “The Voice: Celebrity” will be revealed at a later time.
However, NBC shared that the stars competing will be actors, musicians, influencers, athletes, comedians and reality television stars.
What Is the New Format for ‘The Voice: Celebrity’?
“The Voice: Celebrity” will follow the same format as the original “The Voice.” The contestants will participate in the blind auditions, hoping for a coach to turn their chair.
They will then be placed into teams and mentored by their coaches to try and make it to the next round as viewers vote for their favorites.
When Does ‘The Voice: Celebrity’ Premiere?
A premiere date has yet to be announced, but expect to see “The Voice: Celebrity” in 2027.

title: Hannah Einbinder Challenges Jenna to a Scream-Off on TODAY
summary: Hannah Einbinder just schooled Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones on the art of screaming.
story: Hannah Einbinder just schooled Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones on the art of screaming.

The actor got a lot of practice letting out her inner rage while filming her new movie “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” and she was happy to share some tricks of the trade while appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle Aug. 4.
During the interview, Jenna complimented Einbinder on her screaming abilities, calling her a “scream queen.”
To develop her screaming skills, Einbinder said she went to a Reiki healer.
“Did you know you were blocked there?” Jenna asked.
“I didn’t. I just feel like as a person, I experienced anger and immediately it turned to sadness. Like I wasn’t able to really exercise my rage,” Einbinder said.
Sheinelle, who admitted that she’s never really been able to scream, was curious to know if Einbinder thinks screaming helps release pent up anger.
“I do,” Einbinder said. “And I think if you find it hard to really scream, that’s also information to perhaps kind of ask why you don’t have access to that part of your voice.”
After undergoing vocal chord surgery, Sheinelle didn’t attempt to scream, but Jenna was up for an exercise with Einbinder.
“I’m perimenopausal so the rage is just (there),” Jenna joked.
Einbinder encouraged viewers to join in and instructed Jenna on how to let out her inner rage.
“We’re gonna take a deep breath in and out, and then another deep breath in, and then we’re gonna let it rock,” she said.
When the time came to scream, Jenna began to join Einbinder, but was overshadowed by the actor’s guttural sound. Sheinelle covered her ears to block out the noise.
The co-hosts were left speechless. Sheinelle and a few crew members applauded Einbinder.
“Feels like I’m the only one who did it,” the actor teased. “It feels like y’all were gonna do it with me.”
“Your scream was so (impressive). I had to live in her scream. I was starting and then I just opened my mouth and let your words come out of me,” Jenna said.
At least the exercise paid off for Einbinder.
“I have to tell you, I feel amazing,” she said.

title: Read With Jenna’s August 2026 Pick Is ‘The Perfect Summer Read’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager’s August 2026 Read With Jenna pick is “Sunlight Finds You” by Laura Moriarty.
story: Jenna Bush Hager says her August 2026 Read With Jenna pick, “Sunlight Finds You” by Laura Moriarty, is “the perfect summer read.”
“It is propulsive and drenched in light, just like the title,” she says.
The novel opens in 1949 in St. Petersburg, Florida. There, 17-year-old Nora meets and falls in love with Leonard, a New York transplant.

“His parents, and a secret, separate them which leads Nora through a twisty path towards adulthood, heartbreak and eventually, healing,” Jenna said, calling this a book about “forgiveness, both of ourselves and others, and love.”
"Sunlight Finds You" by Laura Moriarty
Moriarty is the author of multiple novels including “The Chaperone,” which became a movie directed by “Downton Abbey” creator Julian Fellowes in 2018.
With her latest, she always knew she wanted to write a love story — “a big love story.”
“Not exactly a romance, but a story about the way love can change a person and alter the course of the life,” she tells TODAY.com.

Moriarty says she also “knew pretty early” that she wanted to set the novel in St. Petersburg in the 1950s. During WWII, soldiers passed through St. Petersburg on their way to Europe. Some returned permanently upon their return, turning St. Pete into a “boom town,” Moriarty explains.
“It really became this place of explosive growth and typically seeking the sun in good times after the war,” Moriarty says.

But the journey to “Sunlight Finds You” was a long road, she says, because of her own health. Moriarty was diagnosed with cancer while writing the book and had to have her jaw almost completely reconstructed during treatment.
“It slowed me down. I’m so, so happy to be on the other side of it,” she says.
Moriarty says her procedure helped her connect more deeply to Nora and her troubles.
“I started thinking about you know how going through something isolating and hard can make you more vulnerable for a while before it makes wiser,” she says.
She spoke to her mom, who lived in Florida in the 1950s, for context about Laura’s life and the choices women in that era had to face.
“It was really hard to navigate this narrow path for women and girls. They have the same dreams and desires for autonomy that we all do. I don’t want to go back,” she says.
While reading, Moriarty hopes people look back at the crossroads in their lives, including moments they might consider to be mistakes.
“What I really love about her is she’s able to look at her mistakes with her younger self of compassion. She doesn’t go into just beating herself up, or she learns to stop doing that,” she says.

“I hope it prompts people to think about their own big choices that they they made and how it shaped their life. And I hope they can think about doing it with that same sort of compassion. In her case, it made her more compassionate to other people.”

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Episode 4 Delivers Emotional Double Elimination
summary: The latest “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” episode, which aired Aug. 3, saw two contestants eliminated.
story: Warning: This article contains spoilers for “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” Episode 4

Fans are just a few weeks away from finding out which new pro will be competing on Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars,” airing this fall, after the latest round of emotional eliminations on the spinoff series.

The relief the “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” contestants felt last week after learning there wouldn’t be an elimination was short-lived when they were told in Episode 4, which aired Aug. 3, that two of them would be going home.

“DWTS” pro Jenna Johnson arrived to inform the remaining eight dancers that for their next challenge they had to master a key element every performance needs: chemistry. She, along with judges Shirley and Mark Ballas, asked the contestants to pair up and create a steamy routine that showcased a genuine connection with their partner.

Johnson noted that even if the contestants don’t feel passion with their partner, they should make the audience believe in the romance and the story. The duo who weren’t as convincing, would be sent home.
Who survived and made it to the top six? Read a recap of “DWTS: The Next Pro” Episode 4, below.
What Happened During Episode 4 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’

Jenna’s grand entrance onto the ballroom floor featured a “spicy” routine with a man who wasn’t her husband and fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy, as host Robert Irwin pointed out before the challenge was explained.
“When two people dance together, chemistry is critical,” Jenna told the contestants. She challenged them to “build a performance so intimate it will send pulses racing.”
Shirley informed the dancers that they would either perform the rumba or the Argentine tango. The contestants were given two days to craft their routines.

To determine the pairs, Jenna had all the contestants dance with each other in “‘The Next Pro’ version of speed dating.” Then, it was time to select partners. The ladies were asked to choose first. As Nina Mayster and Stephani Sosa both picked Allen Genkin, he had the final say.
Allen Genkin and Nina MaysterAdele Zaikman and AJ PritchardStephani Sosa and Tristan SandersSelena Hamilton and Erik Linder
Allen Genkin and Nina Mayster
Adele Zaikman and AJ Pritchard
Stephani Sosa and Tristan Sanders
Selena Hamilton and Erik Linder

Tristan, who wasn’t initially chosen by any of the ladies, looked visibly affected by not being Stephani’s first choice. He said in his confessional interview that he thought they were “close” and he was surprised by her decision. She explained that she had already danced with Tristan during the competition and wanted to switch it up.
Tristan and Stephani and AJ and Adele randomly chose rumba for their dance. Allen and Nina and Stephani and Tristan selected Argentine tango.
In addition to rehearsals, the duos were told they would get to spend time together outside of the studio. Jenna also revealed one couple would go home in a double elimination.
On their days out together, each contestant opened up about how they fell in love with dance and how much the competition means to them.

On performance day, AJ and Adele were the first couple to dance. Shirley called Adele a “superstar” after the performance but said AJ was too “formed.” Jenna applauded the couple for listening to the feedback she gave them in rehearsals. Mark was more critical, saying the beginning was “bumpy” for him.

Up next were Selena and Erik with their Argentine tango. After they hit their final pose, Jenna let out an excited scream and Shirley said she needed a fan. “I am speechless!” Jenna told the two. “Erik, who are you?” she asked.
He replied, “I’m him.”

Jenna applauded both of them and said she would like to dance with Erik in the future. Mark added that Selena redeemed herself from her bottom two performance last episode. He also said Erik was turning the competition into a “fist fight” with his powerful dancing. Shirley was equally complimentary, giving the two a standing ovation.

Tristan and Stephani followed with their rumba. For his feedback, Mark began with the positives, noting that the two interpreted the lyrics of Sombr’s “Back to Friends” well. But he said the routine needed more “stillness.” His mom agreed, criticizing them for having “enough choreography for two rumbas.” While Jenna praised Stephani for being a “gorgeous” dancer, she told her there was a “fire” missing, causing the contestant to become emotional. Jenna assured Stephani that she is capable and just needs to own her confidence.

Rounding out the dances this week were Allen and Nina with their Argentine tango. Jenna said she was “captivated” by Nina’s moves and her chemistry with Allen. Shirley said she was “confused” because she spotted tango, rumba and samba steps but the routine lacked traditional Argentine tango content. Although Mark agreed that the routine needed more Argentine tango, he said the performance was Nina’s best dance so far.
Who Were the Bottom 2 Couples?
The two couples that failed to exude enough chemistry were Tristan and Stephani and Allen and Nina.

Mark said Tristan and Stephani were “in and out of the chemistry of the dance” and that some moments felt “frantic.” While announcing that Allen and Nina were also in the bottom, Shirley emphasized that the next pro “needs to understand the brief.”
Who Was Eliminated in Episode 4 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?

Before revealing the eliminated couple, Jenna said she was impressed by all the couples and was heartbroken that two dancers had to leave. Shirley called out Allen and Nina for bending the rules too far with their routine. She said based on their performance she was unsure if they would be able to teach a proper Argentine tango. Mark echoed Jenna’s feedback that all the performances were well done. But he said they had reached the halfway point of the competition and that the critiques would be harder.
Shirley revealed that Tristan and Stephani had danced for the last time on the show.

Tristan and Stephani said they were proud of each other and had an emotional goodbye. In her final confessional, Stephani shared that she thought her journey was “cut too short” but that she needed to let go of the “DWTS” chapter of her life. She added that she would never get in her own way again.
Tristan told Robert that he was honored to be in the company of legends and champions, and that he was grateful for the experience.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Just six dancers are left. The next episode of “DWTS: The Next Pro” will air Monday, Aug. 10.

In the upcoming episode, guest judge and “DWTS” champion Daniella Karagach will stop by to challenge the remaining contestants to create “their own unique, wow moves.” The teaser hinted that the pressure might get to a few dancers as they face another elimination.

title: Dominic Sessa Doesn’t Idolize Anthony Bourdain. It’s Why He Could Play Him
summary: Dominic Sessa speaks to TODAY.com about making Tony the movie.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Dominic Sessa arrives at the Orange Room, TODAY.com’s backstage content space at Studio 1A, wearing corduroy pants and a sweater vest. He paces as he waits for his TODAY segment. For Sessa, who plays the late chef, author and television personality Anthony Bourdain in A24’s latest biopic, the stakes have never been higher.

Bourdain, who died in 2018, remains a household name for chefs and casual diners alike. His culinary travel shows (like “Parts Unknown” and “No Reservations”) brought audiences to far-flung places in pursuit of delicious meals and the connection they make possible.

“Tony,” the first studio film from Matt Johnson, takes audiences through a singular summer in a 19-year-old Bourdain’s life, based on the opening chapters of Bourdain’s memoir, “Kitchen Confidential,” which catapulted him to fame. Working at a restaurant in Cape Cod, the Bourdain introduced in “Tony” is pursuing purpose and prominence, leaning on a deceitful “fake it ‘till you make it” mentality until he has a rude awakening courtesy of the kitchen heat.

Sessa, during his TODAY interview, said he thinks he was “type-cast” to play Bourdain. Now 23, Sessa was first plucked from boarding school to play opposite Paul Giamatti in the Oscar-nominated movie “The Holdovers” in 2023. Until that point, he had never acted on camera.

“At times, especially in high school, I was very kind of outlandish and didn’t really operate with integrity. That’s kind of how this character is introduced in the film,” Sessa said during his TODAY chat with Sheinelle Jones on July 27.
Like the late Bourdain once did, Sessa now finds himself ascending in a career that demands confidence right out of the gate. TODAY.com caught up with him ahead of the movie’s release.

For me, the biggest thing was putting yourself in a risky environment. That was something I was actually really familiar with as a young person. When I went to high school, I didn’t really have a solid sense of self and was role-playing a lot of different people and personalities. Then I started acting, and it was the first time that I had to really operate with genuine integrity. Similarly, at least in this movie, Tony inserting himself in that environment where lying and not being true to yourself is what’s going to destroy you.

That was definitely difficult. That was the one thing that I really prepped for the movie, and I think it’s really symbolic of the film. You can’t force it open, or else it’s just ruined, and you have to act with a certain level of care and assertiveness to open an oyster successfully.

One hundred percent. He worked at a few different restaurants in Provincetown. One of them that we frequented is called Ciro & Sal’s. A lot of the people that worked there, the owner at the time, worked with (Bourdain) when he was there in the ‘70s. That was invaluable information. Just to talk to people who actually worked with him in the kitchen and saw him.

I don’t know. I think Matt (Johnson) and I just have really similar sentiments about the world, and especially about being a young man. I think he saw himself in me in a lot of ways. As much as this was a life-changing kind of experience for me, I think equally for him. He learned a lot about himself.

I don’t think we would have been able to make it if we were coming from a point of already being huge fans of Bourdain. I think the fact that this was both of our entry point into learning about him and discovering him is what makes it feel grounded and genuine and why it’s not trying to be this pedestal for this person that we’re idolizing. I don’t think we would have been able to come at it from a genuine place if that were the case.

I think just leading with the truth. Being honest and being OK with not being a fully formed person yet. I think I’m at this age where I, and for a lot of young people as well, want to be respected, want status that you haven’t necessarily earned yet. Learning the right way to do that and to actually understand your potential is life-changing.

title: Ella Rubin Shares the Advice from Anne Hathaway ‘We Could All Use’
summary: After working with Anne Hathaway in the 2024 film “The Idea of You,” Ella Rubin walked away with a valuable life lesson.
story: After working with Anne Hathaway in the 2024 film “The Idea of You,” Ella Rubin walked away with a valuable life lesson.

On Aug. 3, the 24-year-old joined TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle to discuss her new TV series, “Sterling Point.” She also reflected on her breakout role as Izzy, Hathaway’s character’s teen daughter, in “The Idea of You.”

“On set, it was kind of one of the first times that I’d had that much responsibility in a role, and I’d never really done anything like that. And she was really wonderful, just in general, wonderful with me,” Rubin said.
The young actor also divulged the piece of advice Hathaway gave her while they were filming the movie.

“(She) really encouraged me to apologize less unnecessarily,” Rubin said. “This person who’s my hero telling me like, this is not only harmful to you personally but also to your work and to the people around you.

“When you’re a leader on a set, you don’t want other women especially to feel like that’s something that they have to do,” she added. “And so I really took that with me from someone I trust and respect so much.”
Sheinelle Jones personally connected with these words of wisdom.
“I feel like we could all use that advice,” she said.
“Someone walked into my hotel room this morning and I went, ‘Sorry!’” Rubin recalled.
“Yeah, we gotta rewire,” Sheinelle added.
Rubin played Hathaway’s onscreen daughter in “The Idea of You,” and Sheinelle and guest co-host Dylan Dreyer couldn’t help but applaud the casting choice.

“Sheinelle and I sat down and ... we start staring at you and we’re like, ‘It makes so much sense that you played Anne Hathaway’s daughter.’ I mean, the resemblance is uncanny seeing you in person,” Dylan told the actor.
“Well, that is my favorite compliment ever (and) the best comparison, most flattering comparison to get. And she’s also the greatest person,” Rubin said.
Rubin added that she soaked up everything Hathaway said on set.
“Everything she told me I try to remember,” she said.

title: Craig Melvin and Wife Lindsay Czarniak Share a Moment on TODAY That Had the Other Anchors Swooning
summary: Craig Melvin had a sweet message for his wife, Lindsay Czarniak, when she stopped by Studio 1A to talk about her latest project.
story: Craig Melvin had a sweet message for his wife, Lindsay Czarniak, when she stopped by Studio 1A to talk about her latest project.

Czarniak, an Emmy Award-winning sports broadcaster, appeared on the 3rd Hour of TODAY Aug. 3 to promote her new true crime series “Game Day Murders,” which highlights high-profile murder investigations in the sports world.
The couple’s chemistry was evident during the segment. Craig joked that it was “not awkward at all” interviewing his wife, though his body language signaled the opposite.
“You feel funny?” Czarniak asked.
“I do feel funny,” Craig said.
Given Craig’s prior experience on “Dateline,” guest co-host Savannah Sellers asked if he offered his wife any advice while she was prepping to film her new series.
“No,” he replied. “By the way, I give her no tips. I’ve been married for 15 years. No tips.”
“That’s not true!”
“Well,” Craig said.
“I mean, you’re a great sounding board,” Czarniak said.
The journalist went on to say she did discuss the show with Craig.

“I think one thing that I found really eye-opening was the process. We did talk about that a lot because this is my first time being around this type of show. I was so just blown away by the producers and what they do day in and day out, how they get families to talk,” she said.
Craig briefly agreed but seemed keen on keeping the interview going — and his wife called him out on it.
“No? You’re moving on,” she said.
“Well, no, because I want to make sure ... c’mon, this isn’t, we don’t have three hours, sweetie,” he said.
“OK, but I just thought you could interject,” Czarniak teased.
“We’re just here,” Savannah joked, suggesting that she and Dylan Dreyer were just flies on the wall of Craig and Czarniak’s playful banter.
During the segment, the TODAY team surprised Czarniak with a message from Shaquille O’Neal, who serves as executive producer on “Game Day Murders.”
Afterwards, Craig shared his own short but sweet praise of his wife’s work.
“I’m proud of you,” he said.
A collective “Aww” was heard from Czarniak, Savannah and Dylan Dreyer at that point. Then, Czarniak teased her husband, saying, “Was that recorded?”
“Oh, I’ll hear about it forever,” Craig joked.
“This was so fun to have you here. I love watching Craig blush,” Dylan said.
Savannah agreed, saying, “I know, it’s really cute.”
Dylan, who was about to fill in as a guest co-host on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, asked Czarniak if she’d stick around for the rest of the 3rd Hour of TODAY in her place.
“No!” Craig joked.
“Yes!” Lindsay replied.
“And I’ll third wheel,” Savannah said.
“When they do the sweetie talk, you will feel like the third wheel,” Dylan joked.
Fans of the couple can get more of their sweet banter in the latest episode of Craig’s podcast, “Glass Half Full,” since Czarniak was the guest.

title: Ariana Grande to Step Away from Public Life Amid ‘Endless, Ongoing’ Scrutiny
summary: Ariana Grande plans to take a break from life in the spotlight after finishing her “Eternal Sunshine Tour,” her rep said in a statement.
story: Just days after the release of her eighth studio album, Ariana Grande revealed plans to take a break from life in the spotlight.
A representative for the singer said in a statement the 33-year-old “will be taking a step back from visibility” when her “Eternal Sunshine Tour” wraps up Sept. 1.

“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” the statement said.

Grande did not reveal when she intends to return to public life. In July, it was announced she exited her role in Season 13 of “American Horror Story” due to scheduling conflicts with her tour, per Deadline.
The performer also backed out of her planned appearance in a summer 2027 revival of Stephen Sondheim’s musical “Sunday in the Park with George.”
The official X account for the production confirmed on Aug. 2 that Grande would no longer be in the production.
“We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support,” the statement read.

The production of “Sunday in the Park with George,” which was originally announced in January, will still open at the Barbican in summer 2027 “as planned” and casting “will be announced in due course.” The X account’s bio states Jonathan Bailey will still star.

In Grande’s new album, “Petal,” she speaks about the complications of fame, including the intense scrutiny that comes with being a public figure. The singer told Apple Music she wrote the album from a place of “unfiltered rage.”

The New York Times penned a review of the album and suggested that Grande sounded “irritated with the invasive nature of fame” throughout “Petal.” Grande has been the subject of numerous headlines in recent years, often about her love life and physical appearance.

Grande has addressed public scrutiny of her body on multiple occasions. In November 2025, the singer shared a video to her Instagram story of an old interview with co-star Cynthia Erivo, in which they’re asked about beauty standards and critics.
“I’ve heard every version of it, of what’s wrong with me, and then you fix it, and then it’s wrong for different reasons,” Grande said at the time.
The singer went on to explain the dangers of speculating about other people’s health and criticizing their bodies.

“I think in today’s society, there’s a comfortability that we shouldn’t have at all commenting on others’ looks, appearance, what they think is going on behind the scenes or health, or how they present themselves. From what you’re wearing to your body, to your face, to your everything,  there’s a comfortability that people have commenting on that that I think is really dangerous. And I think it’s dangerous for all parties involved,” she said.

title: Trump administration revokes Brazilian ambassador’s visa in diplomatic dispute
summary: The Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil’s U.S. ambassador Tuesday — the latest jab in a monthslong diplomatic spat between the two countries.
story: The Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil’s U.S. ambassador Tuesday — the latest jab in a monthslong diplomatic spat between the two countries.

The U.S. action was taken in retaliation for Brazil’s withholding formal approval for the Trump administration’s pick for U.S. ambassador to Brazil, Florida House Speaker Daniel Perez, a senior State Department official told reporters Tuesday.
The official, who spoke on behalf of the State Department on condition of anonymity, said Brazil has indicated the approval is likely to be delayed until after its election in October.
The Brazilian government said it repudiates the visa revocation of their ambassador, calling both justifications from the U.S. “false,” and noted that the U.S. request remains under review.

“It should be recalled that individual sanctions against Brazilian officials remain in force, notably the cancellation of U.S. visas based on the unfounded allegation that former President Bolsonaro is being subjected to political persecution,” the office of the president of Brazil said in a statement. “Those affected include Supreme Court justices and senior members of the Executive Branch.”
Jair Bolsonaro was the president of Brazil before President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

The Brazilian president’s office said the decision “is not an isolated incident,” and “forms part of a deliberate escalation of hostile measures against Brazil, driven by ideological motives that are incompatible with a bilateral partnership that has always been guided by mutual respect.”

The tit-for-tat has been ongoing since at least March, when Brazil denied visas to a U.S. delegation traveling to a critical minerals forum, the U.S. official said. In July, Brazil also denied visas to two U.S. officials, accusing them of plotting to meddle in Brazil’s electoral process.
“This week we had to deny visas to two young folks they were sending to Brazil to meddle in Brazil’s elections,” Lula said at an event last Wednesday.

The senior State Department official denied the accusations and said the assistant secretary for democracy, human rights and labor, Riley M. Barnes, and one of his deputies, Samuel Samson, “were making a routine trip” and were “denied the ability to do routine, common work between the two countries.”

“We’ve taken reciprocal action with respect to the Brazilian diplomat here to make the point that it can’t always be one-sided,” the senior State Department official said. “If there’s going to be limitations on one side’s diplomats, they will be reciprocated.”

The official clarified that Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti will not be expelled from the U.S. but warned that additional diplomatic options remain on the table if the Brazilian government continues to delay or refuse to approve the U.S. ambassador nominee. If Viotti leaves the country, she would need to reapply for a visa, the official said, adding that the Brazilian ambassador’s visa will be reinstated if Brazil approves Perez.

“We communicated continually with the Brazilian government for weeks and have given the Brazilian government every opportunity to do the right thing, yet they have continually delayed and obfuscated,” the official said. “President Trump has the right to determine who represents the American people and interests around the world.”

“President Trump is assembling an America First diplomatic A-team across his administration, subject to the advice and consent of the Senate. We reject any effort by foreign countries to interfere in our domestic processes,” the official added.

title: Trump claims Iran talks are underway as Tehran denies it
summary: The international oil benchmark Brent crude rose again to 2.7% with traffic through the crucial waterway at a trickle compared with its peacetime flow.
story: President Donald Trump accused Iran of duplicity and insisted the two sides were discussing reopening the Strait of Hormuz as early as Tuesday, even as Tehran denied talks were even taking place.

The diplomatic confusion was underscored by an attack on a cargo vessel near the strait’s Oman coast, as reported by the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center, an organization run by the British navy that helps protect commercial shipping in high-risk areas.

With traffic through the bottleneck still at a trickle of its peacetime flow, the international oil benchmark Brent crude rose again by 2.7% Tuesday, reflecting uncertainty in the market rather than any confidence in the diplomatic process.

title: Video shows moment drone burst into fireball on Russian beach
summary: Ukraine didn’t deny launching the drone but said the Kremlin’s air defenses had shot it down and that “it was Putin who killed these Russians.”
story: The beach was packed, many vacationers lounging near the turquoise waters when the drone slammed into the white sand and burst into a fireball.

Russian officials said seven people, including three children, were killed and 58 others injured by the explosion in the Black Sea resort town of Gelendzhik on Monday. The explosion was captured on video, which was shared on social media and verified by NBC News.

Moscow accused Ukraine of targeting civilians, which would constitute a war crime, and unleashed a barrage of aerial strikes on its neighbor. Ukraine’s attacks inside Russia come as its own civilians faced deadly Russian bombardment throughout the summer.
Ukrainian officials did not confirm they were responsible, but they also did not deny it.

“What happened today was a deliberate strike by the Kyiv regime against the civilian population — people who have absolutely no connection to military infrastructure,” Veniamin Kondratyev, the governor of the Krasnodar region, said on his official Telegram channel. “There can be no justification for such a cynical and inhumane terrorist act targeting children.”

The explosion comes amid a concerted Ukrainian effort to push the war’s front line closer than ever to Moscow, with strikes targeting shipping vessels, oil sites, warehouses and ammunition depots in recent weeks.

Since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched his large-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Kyiv has honed an innovative and lethal strategy of using cheaply manufactured drones as it seeks to pressure Moscow into a peace settlement. Some hit their targets, while others are often shot down.
Between July 24 and July 31, at least 61 people were killed and more than 320 wounded in Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said Friday.

After the explosion in Gelendzhik, Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council’s Center for Countering Disinformation, said: “Russian air defense shot down a drone onto people lying on the beach.”
“It was Putin who killed these Russians,” he said in a statement. “Had he not started the war and the strikes on Ukraine, they would be alive.”
Kovalenko also accused Putin of downplaying Ukrainian attacks on Russia, creating an “illusion of peace” that has made the public complacent.
“Had they acknowledged the war on their own territory, people would have reacted more actively to the alert, which in some places in Russia is not even announced,” he said.
A separate attack had also hit a warehouse in Leningrad, its regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said early Tuesday.

title: East Asia is baking in ‘cruelly hot’ summer
summary: A deadly heat wave is gripping large parts of East Asia, bringing the hottest temperature on record in South Korea and complicating earthquake recovery efforts in Japan.
story: A deadly heat wave is gripping large parts of East Asia, bringing the hottest temperature on record in South Korea and complicating earthquake recovery efforts in Japan.
Extreme heat has been linked to 19 deaths in South Korea since mid-May, with President Lee Jae Myung calling it a national disaster Tuesday.
“We need to make efforts for ​a fundamental overhaul of the national crisis system, ‌since this extreme weather is becoming normal,” he said at a Cabinet meeting.
On Sunday, temperatures hit 42.5 degrees Celsius (108 degrees Fahrenheit) in the southeastern city of Yangsan, the highest in 122 years of record-keeping.

title: Trump calls Iranian leadership ‘extremely duplicitous’ after Tehran denies new talks will start Monday
summary: Iran said it wasn’t holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz.
story: President Donald Trump branded the Iranian regime “unbelievably duplicitous,” saying Iranian officials asked for talks on ending the war only to announce that no discussions would be held.

Trump had earlier said that the United States and Iran will hold new discussions Monday afternoon, after he called off intense new strikes to allow for a deal on the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran’s nuclear program.
However, Iran said it was not holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the strait.

“We currently do not have negotiations with America,” and Iran has no plans to host foreign delegations or send negotiators abroad in the coming days, Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters.

Trump later took to Truth Social, where he wrote: “Iranian Leadership is unbelievably duplicitous! They ask for a meeting, some would say ‘beg,’ talks begin, with more scheduled in the immediate future, and they say, openly and proudly, that they’re not having any discussions, that nothing is being talked about, and they’re only dealing with ‘Oman.’”
Iran did not immediately respond to his comments.
Trump later told reporters at the White House after his post on Truth Social that talks with Iran were taking place.

“They’re going on right now. It’s an amazing thing we have a little problem with Iran because we have many talks, and we’ll say we have or we don’t have. You know, we’re straight about it, but they deny it,” Trump said. “But they’re not denying it now. They just put out a statement not denying it.”
Trump also told reporters that the Strait of Hormuz will be open to marine traffic Tuesday.

“We’re talking about the strait, the opening of the strait, having it open literally by tomorrow, completely open, and that’s phase one,” Trump said, saying the second phase of talks would focus on Iran’s nuclear program.
Time is running out for Iran to make a deal, according to Trump.
“This is a last chance for them to sign a good document,” Trump said, adding, “I want to give them every last chance before decapitation.”
Trump had said Sunday that he agreed to call off the attacks amid what he said were the “parameters of a deal” that would include resuming shipping through the key global trade route.

Speaking on Air Force One, Trump said the canceled strikes were going to be “the biggest attack since World War II.” The president said that the U.S. was “holding” what would have been a “massive attack,” but that it could still take place “anytime we want.”
Trump, however, said that Iran does not have a deadline to come to an agreement.

title: U.S. agrees to pause attacks on Iran subject to ‘rapidly’ making deal, Trump says
summary: The deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Tehran’s “nuclear threat,” the president said.
story: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” that would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“We have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social. “This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s  nuclear threat.”
The president said the U.S. was “locked and loaded and ready to go” but that he agreed to cancel attacks “subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.”
He added that Israel, the U.S. partner in the war with Iran, “joins me in this commitment.”
“Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE,” Trump said of a possible new agreement.

The statement came after the State Department on Saturday urged Americans across the Middle East to consider leaving the region or be prepared to depart on short notice. It also warned of flight disruptions and security risks as the conflict with Iran appeared to be escalating.

Trump earlier threatened Iran with additional attacks, saying Friday that the U.S. will be “hitting them very hard,” while Iran has vowed to “punish” the U.S. and both nations traded what some U.S. officials described as “heavy” strikes.
Responding to Trump’s announcement, Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told “Meet the Press” Sunday that the president should not trust Iran’s word.
Asked why a fresh deal would be different when the memorandum of understanding signed in June failed, he told moderator Kristen Welker: “Well, it may not be.”
“We only have three choices: escalate, retreat and come home, or maintain the status quo. I would maintain the status quo as long as I could,” he said.
Iran’s acting minister of defense, Majid Ibn al-Reza, meanwhile said that U.S. remarks should be viewed as “psychological and cognitive warfare.”
He said on X that the threat of further strikes would be taken “as the basis for increasing readiness, strengthening deterrence, and enhancing our own power.”

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, a key regional player, spoke with Trump by phone Saturday. According to the Saudi state news agency, he told him that dialogue was needed to de-escalate Middle East tensions, and expressed concerns over plans for new strikes against Iran.
The State Department issued fresh security guidance Saturday for Americans in the region.

“Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions,” the State Department said. “Some airlines in the region have postponed resumption of earlier flight schedules; others have cancelled some routes. Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation.”
The State Department also urged Americans to reconsider travel bans to or through the region.
The warning was distributed through U.S. embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

The agency posted a nearly identical statement earlier this month, but that bulletin did not urge Americans to prepare to leave the Middle East or to reconsider upcoming trips, reflecting Washington’s growing concern that the conflict could widen.
On Saturday, the Kuwait army said its air defense systems intercepted drone attacks from Iran.

“Kuwaiti air defenses are currently engaging hostile drone attacks following the Iranian aggression. The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosions heard are a result of air defense systems intercepting the hostile attacks,” the army said.

Earlier in the week, the U.S. military confirmed it had executed a “heavy wave of strikes” on Iran, hours after Fox News reported that the president in a phone call had vowed to “beat the f-----g s--- out of” the country.
Trump has grown increasingly exasperated with the state of the war, one Trump ally told NBC News.
“There was not a real strategy for how long or what they should do to get to the endpoint,” the ally said.
The conflict has now entered its sixth month, despite Trump’s repeated early predictions that the war would resolve itself “shortly.”
The protracted conflict has led to soaring oil prices globally and rising gas prices in the U.S.
There was a brief reprieve from fighting in June when the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding outlining the process for talks to end the war.
But in early July, Trump declared a ceasefire to be “over,” and the countries resumed striking targets in the Middle East.
